checks.requirement: The laboratory director or designee reviews all technical policies and procedures at least every two years.
checks.subject: Policy and Procedure Review
checks.note:
NOTE: The laboratory director must ensure that the collection of testing policies and technical procedures is complete, current, and has been thoroughly reviewed by a knowledgeable person. Technical approaches must be scientifically valid and clinically relevant. 
  
  To minimize the burden on the laboratory and reviewer(s), the CAP suggests using a schedule whereby roughly 1/24 of all technical policies and procedures are reviewed monthly. Paper/electronic signature review must be at the level of each procedure, or as multiple signatures on a listing of named procedures. A single signature on a Title Page or Index is not a sufficient record that each policy or procedure has been carefully reviewed. Signature or initials on each page of a policy or procedure is not required. 
  
  The laboratory may record review of electronic procedures by: 
  
  * Including statements such as
checks.evidence_of_compliance:
Evidence of Compliance: 
  
  * Records of policy or procedure review
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Non-Compliant. While the laboratory has established a Quality Manual (0XYZ0001.0Rev3-Quality Manual2025.pdf) and Quality Management Review Process (A1003.0-Quality Management Review Process.pdf), there is no evidence provided of a biennial review log or individual procedure sign-offs as required by COM.10100. The search summary indicates that standard operating procedures (GS series) are reviewed biennially, but the actual records of these reviews were not retrieved. Per the requirement note, a single signature on a title page or index is insufficient; the laboratory must provide documentation demonstrating that each technical policy and procedure has been reviewed by the director or designee within the last two years. Currently, no such records are available for verification.
corrective_actions: 1) Establish a biennial review schedule for all technical policies and procedures, ensuring 1/24 of the documents are reviewed monthly.

2) Implement a tracking log or electronic signature system that captures the reviewer's name and date for each individual procedure, ensuring compliance with the requirement that index-level signatures are insufficient.
checks.ai_evidence_summary: **COM.10100**: The laboratory director or designee must review all technical policies and procedures at least every two years. This review ensures the collection of testing policies and technical procedures is complete, current, and thoroughly reviewed by a knowledgeable person, confirming scientific validity and clinical relevance. Standard operating procedures (GS series), excluding instrument maintenance procedures (FS series), are reviewed biennially. Other documents are reviewed periodically to ensure they remain correct, complete, and current. Review of electronic procedures can be recorded by including statements like "reviewed by [name of reviewer] on [date of review]" in the electronic record. A single signature on a Title Page or Index is not sufficient evidence of careful review for each policy or procedure.

checks.requirement: The laboratory director reviews and approves all new technical policies and procedures, as well as substantial changes to existing documents, before implementation.
checks.subject: New Policy and Procedure Approval
checks.note:
NOTE: This review may not be delegated to designees in laboratories subject to the CLIA regulations. 
  
  Paper or electronic signature review of records is acceptable. A secure electronic signature is desirable, but not required.
checks.evidence_of_compliance:
Evidence of Compliance: 
  
  * Records of new policy or procedure approval
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Non-Compliant. While the '0XYZ0001.0Rev3-Quality Manual2025' (referenced in search_summary) establishes a policy requiring the laboratory director to approve new technical policies and procedures, no actual records of such approvals were provided in the retrieved documents. The requirement explicitly mandates that the laboratory director must review and approve all new technical policies and procedures, and this duty cannot be delegated for CLIA-regulated laboratories. The current evidence set contains job descriptions ('D1001.1V3-Lab Director Job Description and Responsibility.pdf') and general IQCP templates, but lacks the specific signature-verified records of policy/procedure approval required by COM.10200.
corrective_actions: 1) Implement a formal document control log or electronic signature system to capture and archive the laboratory director's approval for all new and substantially revised technical procedures.
2) Conduct a retrospective audit of all current technical SOPs to ensure each bears evidence of the laboratory director's signature and date of approval.
3) Ensure all future document revisions include a signature page or electronic audit trail demonstrating the laboratory director's direct review and approval prior to implementation.
cited_documents: D1001.1V3-Lab Director Job Description and Responsibility.pdf
checks.ai_evidence_summary: **COM.10200**: The laboratory director is responsible for approving new technical policies and procedures, as well as substantial changes to existing documents. This approval cannot be delegated for laboratories subject to CLIA regulations. The Quality Manual, 0XYZ0001.0Rev3-Quality Manual2025, states that new documents and those with significant changes are reviewed by an authorized person and approved by the laboratory director before use. Policies are reviewed when the relevant CAP checklist is revised or established. Standard operating procedures (GS series), excluding instrument maintenance procedures (FS series), are reviewed biennially. Other documents are reviewed periodically to ensure they remain correct, complete, and current. Records of new policy or procedure approval were not found in the provided documents.

policy_evidence.snippet: The following represents one example of how you might organize your IQCP for QC of a commercial cartridge-based molecular test system for detection of a single or multiple targets. This is based in part on information included in CLSI EP23-A “Laboratory Quality Control Based on Risk Management” and CDC/CMS “Developing an IQCP, A Step-by-Step Guide”. Laboratories should modify this template and examples to support their practice. A unique IQCP should be implemented for each separate method or system. A practical strategy would be to review this example together with materials provided by your manufacturer, your accreditation organization, and CMS when developing an IQCP for QC for a commercial cartridge-based molecular test system. IQCP for QC of molecular test system Simplexa Flu A/B and RSV assay performed on Diasorin LIAISON® MDX Facility: XYZ Laboratory Test System: Diasorin Disc-based Simplexa Flu A/B and RSV molecular test system to test influenza A, influenza B and RSV viruses from nasopharyngeal swab specimen Test System Primary SOPs include: #GS130G.0_Simplexa FluA_B_RSV Direct Gen II SOP Historical Quality Review: CLIA ’88 regulations require performing at least positive and negative QC for each test on each day of use.
policy_evidence.title: XYZ-MOL-Micro-IQCP-Simplexa

Specifically, changes in technical procedures require review and approval by the laboratory director. The Change Request Form, G1007.1_Change Request Form Sample Control, indicates that all changes need approval from the Lab Director or their designee before implementation. management

Document Number： D1001.1 Version #： 3 Author：Wenli Zhou Date of Composition: 11/01/2020 Date of Execution：04/26/2026 Page 1 of 4 1. Objective
Provide the qualification and responsibilities of laboratory director for the high complexity laboratory 2. Qualifications
2.1 MD, DO, or DPM licensed to practice in the jurisdiction where the laboratory is located (if required), and: 1) Certification in anatomic or clinical pathology, or both, by the American Board of Pathology or American
Osteopathic Board of Pathology, or 2) Have at least two years of experience supervising high complexity testing. or 2.2 Doctoral degree (PhD or DPH) in a chemical, biological, or clinical laboratory science from an accredited
institution, and: 1) Have current certification by a board approved by HHS, and 2) Have at least two years of laboratory training or experience or both, and laboratory experience directing or
supervising high complexity testing. 3. Job Duties and Responsibilities
3.1 The laboratory director is responsible for overall operation of the laboratory
3.2 Oversees employment of personnel
3.3 Ensures all duties performed per regulations
3.4 Develops quality system approach for accurate testing
Non-delegated Responsibilities
Director must ensure that:

checks.requirement: The laboratory has records indicating that all personnel are knowledgeable about the contents of the policies and procedures (including changes) relevant to the scope of their testing activities.
checks.subject: Knowledge of Policies and Procedures
checks.note: NOTE: The form of this system is at the discretion of the laboratory director. Annual procedure sign-off by testing personnel is not required.
checks.evidence_of_compliance:
Evidence of Compliance: 
  
  * Records indicating that the testing personnel have read the policies and procedures, new and revised, OR records of another written method approved by the laboratory director
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Partial. The laboratory has established policies for personnel responsibilities and training as evidenced by 'D1001.5V3-Test personnel job description and responsibilities.pdf' and '5-D1001.5V2-Test personnel job description and responsibilities-CW.docx'. While the search summary indicates that personnel participate in and pass required policy and procedure training, the specific records demonstrating that all personnel have read and acknowledged current policies and procedures (or an alternative director-approved method) were not provided in the retrieved documents. The 'K1003.1.5_Data Collection Form for Personnel.docx' is identified as a tool for QA review rather than a record of policy acknowledgement. To achieve full compliance, the laboratory must provide evidence of the specific system used to track personnel acknowledgement of new and revised policies.
corrective_actions: 1) Implement and document a formal system for personnel to acknowledge reading new and revised policies and procedures.
2) Maintain these acknowledgement records in a centralized location to demonstrate compliance during future inspections.
cited_documents: D1001.5V3-Test personnel job description and responsibilities.pdf
checks.ai_evidence_summary: **COM.10300**: The laboratory ensures personnel knowledge of policies and procedures through documented training and competency assessments. All personnel consistently follow policy and protocol, with no deviations recorded in the problem log. Adequate training is provided for new or changed procedures, following a standard laboratory protocol that includes initial learning and performing tests under guidance. Any issues stemming from improper training are addressed with retraining. Testing personnel are responsible for implementing all laboratory procedures and following the laboratory's procedures for specimen handling, processing, test analyses, reporting, and maintaining records. They must also adhere to quality control policies and perform and document all QC activities. The laboratory director delegates responsibilities to testing personnel, who must participate in and pass required policy, instrument/equipment, and standard procedure training. Records of competency assessment for new and existing testing personnel reflect specific skills and evaluation methods.

policy_evidence.document_uri: gs://xyzlapp-inspect-050526/Inspection Documents_2026/Lab Policies/Lab Quality Manual/0XYZ0001.0Rev3-Quality Manual2025.pdf
policy_evidence.snippet:
QUALITY MANUAL Page 15 of 21 6.8 QSE Process Management
Purpose This policy provides direction for the processes and procedures for how the laboratory
manages pre-examination, examination, post-examination, and quality processes to
optimize both effectiveness in meeting requirements and efficiency in use of costly
human and other resources. The laboratory uses process management to transform
policy into action. Analysis, design,
and
documentation
of laboratory
processes New and modified quality and technical processes are assessed for risk and analyzed and
designed to ensure consistent with other laboratory and organization processes, meet
customer expectations, and support adherence to regulatory, accreditation, and XYZ Lab
requirements. All pre-examination, examination, post-examination, and quality processes are
documented with process maps (or flow charts), procedures (instructions), and applicable
forms to communicate to laboratory personnel how to meet regulatory, accreditation,
and customer requirements in the course of performing laboratory work. Measurement uncertainties and biological reference intervals are included in the
documentation for each examination method as appropriate. Process
validation and/or
verification New and modified processes critical to the quality of the laboratory’s services are
validated and/or verified as meeting the laboratory’s needs and intent before
implementation. This applies to all equipment, instruments, analytical systems,
examination methods, reagent kits, and computer systems and their related software
functions.
policy_evidence.title: 0XYZ0001.0Rev3-Quality Manual2025

policy_evidence.snippet:
2.1 Written Policy and standard operating procedures (SOPs): the laboratory shall have written policy and SOP
for every step of the patient sample testing process from sample receiving to reporting as well as for the general
laboratory operations. The SOPs shall be approved by the laboratory director before use. Laboratory director or
its designee shall review SOPs at least once every two years to ensure the procedures are up to date and meet
the requirements of the users. 2.2 Specimen identification and integrity: all specimens shall be identified and labeled (refer to G1001.0 and
GS1001. 0) to ensure accuracy throughout the testing process. 2.3 Complaints Investigation and resolution: all complaints and problems reported to the laboratory shall be
documented, investigated. When necessary, corrective actions shall be taken to resolve the problem. Complaints, investigation process and corresponding corrective actions shall be documented with an
Investigation and Improvement Report Form (refer to B1003.0 and B1003. 1) and monitored for improvement. 2.4 Communications: the laboratory shall document problems that occur as result of breakdowns in
communication between the laboratory and the customers （refer to B1003.0 and B1003.1）. Corrective action
must be taken to resolve the problem and prevent any future occurrence.
policy_evidence.title: A1002.0V2-Quality Planning Process

checks.requirement: The laboratory retains a paper or electronic copy of discontinued policies and procedures with dates of initial use and retirement for at least two years (five years for transfusion medicine).
checks.subject: Discontinued Policies and Procedures
checks.note:
NOTE: The laboratory must follow its document control system to archive discontinued policies and procedures. 
  
  Discontinued policies and procedures must generally be inaccessible to the working areas of the laboratory (GEN.20375). 
  
  For testing on minors (under the age of 21), stricter national, federal, state (or provincial), or local laws and regulations may apply to retention of discontinued policies and procedures.
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Compliant. The laboratory’s document control system, as defined in H1001.0V3-Document Management Program, explicitly mandates that obsolete controlled documents be dated and archived in a designated 'Retired' folder for a minimum of two years. This aligns with the requirements of COM.10500. The search summary confirms that the laboratory maintains both electronic and hard copy archives for discontinued policies and procedures, ensuring they are inaccessible to working areas as required by GEN.20375. The retention period meets the general two-year requirement; however, the laboratory should ensure that any transfusion medicine policies are retained for the required five-year period per the note in COM.10500.
corrective_actions: Continue current practice of archiving obsolete documents in the 'Retired' folder per H1001.0V3-Document Management Program.
Verify that transfusion medicine policies are flagged for a five-year retention period to ensure compliance with the specific note in COM.10500.
checks.ai_evidence_summary: **COM.10500**: The XYZ Lab's Record Management Program, H1002.0V2-Record Management Program, specifies that policies and procedures are retained for at least two years following discontinuance. This is further supported by the Document Management Program, H1001.0V3-Document Management Program, which states that obsolete controlled documents shall be dated and saved in a "Retired" folder on the company server or hard copy folder for at least two years unless otherwise stated. The original copies of policies and standard operating procedures are kept in a shared drive with a backup on an independent hard drive. The hard copy of obsolete documents is to be verified and shredded immediately.

checks.requirement: The laboratory immediately notifies physicians or other clinical personnel responsible for patient care when results of designated tests exceed established "critical" values. Records of notification are retained.
checks.subject: Critical Result Notification
checks.note:
NOTE: Alert or critical results are those results that may require prompt clinical attention to avert significant patient morbidity or mortality. The laboratory director, in consultation with the clinicians served, must define the critical values and critical results that pertain to its patient population. The laboratory may establish different critical results for specific patient subpopulations (for example, dialysis clinic patients). 
  
  An appropriate notification includes a direct dialogue with the responsible individual or an electronic communication (eg, secure email or fax) with confirmation of receipt by the responsible individual. 
  
  For communication of significant and unexpected surgical pathology and cytopathology findings, refer to ANP.12175 and CYP.06450 instead. 
  
  Allowing clinicians to
checks.evidence_of_compliance:
Evidence of Compliance: 
  
  * Records of notification within the established timeframe
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Partial. The laboratory has established policy requirements for critical result notification within 'G1002.0V2-Laboratory Test Standard Operating Procedure Guide', which mandates that testing SOPs include procedures for imminently life-threatening results. Additionally, the search summary indicates that notification protocols for inaccurate results are documented in the test report problem log. However, while the policy framework exists, the laboratory has not provided specific records of notification (e.g., logs of direct dialogue or confirmed electronic communications) to demonstrate consistent adherence to the 'Evidence of Compliance' requirement. The current documentation confirms the existence of a process, but the actual execution records remain unverified.
corrective_actions: 1) Compile and maintain a centralized log of critical result notifications that includes the date, time, person notified, and confirmation of receipt.
2) Conduct a retrospective audit of recent critical results to ensure all notifications were documented in accordance with the policy defined in G1002.0V2.
cited_documents: G1002.0V2-Laboratory Test Standard Operating Procedure Guide.pdf
checks.ai_evidence_summary: **COM.30000**: The laboratory must immediately alert the ordering doctor when test results indicate an imminent life-threatening condition. Test items associated with critical results should be marked in the lab test menu list (G1002.2). A detailed protocol for critical result reporting must be included in the specific reporting SOP, and all findings and communications must be recorded and maintained. The Laboratory Test Standard Operating Procedure Guide (G1002.0V2-Laboratory Test Standard Operating Procedure Guide) specifies that testing SOPs should include "Imminently life-threatening (critical) test results". When errors or inaccurate information are discovered in reported patient test results, the ordering physician or customer must be promptly notified via phone or email, and the notification content, person, and time must be recorded in the test report problem log.

policy_evidence.snippet:
XYZ Lab Document Name Test Report Correction Process XYZ Lab Document Number G1006.0 Version #4 3 Author：XYZ Laboratory Date of Composition：
11/20/2020 Date of Execution of the current version：
04/25/2025 Page 1 of 2 XYZ Laboratory, 2009 Ranch Road 620 N, Suite 325, Lakeway TX, 78734 1. Purpose and application
This document provides standard operating procedures for test report correction 2. Process
When errors or inaccurate information in the reported patient test results are discovered, or update of result interpretation
is made for the report, the laboratory must do the following:
Issue corrected report if patient/customer results need to be corrected. Issue amended report if patient/customer demographic information need to be updated. Issue updated report if patient/customer result interpretation need to be updated. 2.1 Promptly notify the ordering physician or customer via phone or email about the error, inaccurate or updated
information and let them know amended, corrected or updated report will be issued and delivered to them shortly. Record the notification content, person and time in the test report problem log. 2.2 Issue amended, corrected or updated report promptly to the ordering physician, patient/customer.

policy_evidence.snippet:
1.3 If the test is modified from a FDA cleared or approved test including different patient population, instrument model,
software, specimen types, sample preparation method or cutoff values etc, the analytical specification is no longer be
appropriate, the validation plan needs to be in place to confirm all the specifications as for the laboratory-developed test
(LDT). 1.3.1 Clinical performance parameters include clinical validity and clinical utility. 1.3.1.1 Clinical validity includes clinical performance characteristics, such as clinical sensitivity, clinical specificity,
positive and negative predictive value in defined populations or likelihood ratios. 1.3.1.2 In genetic testing, clinical utility begins with demonstration that a particular genetic marker, mutation, or sequence
is associated with a carrier, predisposition to disease, or disease state, or is predictive of therapeutic response. In addition,
clinical utility requires demonstration that this information can positively impact the course of patient management. 1.3.2 Analytical performance parameters include accuracy, precision, reportable range, and reference interval, as well as
analytical sensitivity and limit of detection, analytical specificity, robustness (i.e. specimen stability, reagent stability),
and other important parameters that may affect assay performance (such as linearity, carryover, cross-contamination, as
appropriate and applicable).

policy_evidence.snippet:
Laboratory Test Standard Operating Procedure Guide XYZ Lab Document Name
XYZ Lab Document Number G1002.0 Version 2 Author：XYZ Laboratory Date of Composition: 11/10/2020 Date of the Current Version：11/01/2024 Page 1 of 2 1. Objective
Provide a guidance for constructing laboratory pre-analytical, analytical and postanalytical operating procedure. 2. Testing Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) Requirements
The testing SOP should consist of the following sections 1) Principle and clinical significance of the test 2) Requirements for patient preparation; specimen collection, labeling, storage, preservation, transportation, processing, and referral; and criteria for specimen acceptability and rejection 3) Preparation of slides, solutions, calibrators, controls, reagents, stains, and other materials used in testing. 4) Calibration and calibration verification procedures (procedure calibration). 5) Step-by-step performance of the procedure, including test calculations and interpretation of results 6) Analytic measurement range for test results for the test system, if applicable. 7) Control procedures 8) Corrective action to take when calibration or control results fail to meet the laboratory's criteria for acceptability. 9) Limitations in the test methodology, including interfering substances 10) Reference intervals (normal values) 11) Imminently life-threatening (critical) test results 12) Pertinent literature references

checks.requirement: For verbally communicated critical results, personnel communicating results request and record “read-back” of the results.
checks.subject: Critical Result Read-Back
checks.note: NOTE: If critical results are transmitted electronically (eg, secure email or fax), the laboratory must confirm receipt by the responsible individual; however, no read-back is necessary.
checks.evidence_of_compliance:
Evidence of Compliance: 
  
  * Records of critical result notification, including read-back as necessary
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Non-Compliant. The laboratory lacks documented evidence of a policy or procedure requiring the 'read-back' of verbally communicated critical results as mandated by COM.30100. While the search summary indicates that critical results are tracked, the retrieved documents (XYZ-MOL-Micro-IQCP-Simplexa.docx, G1001.0V3-Laboratory Testing Process Control Plan_2025.pdf, J1004.0-Voluntary Reporting of Adverse Events Policy and Process.pdf) do not contain the required read-back protocol. Furthermore, no records of critical result notifications demonstrating the read-back process were provided for review. The laboratory must establish a formal policy and maintain logs that explicitly capture the read-back confirmation for all verbal critical result communications.

policy_evidence.document_uri: gs://xyzlapp-inspect-050526/Inspection Documents_2026/Lab Operation/D-Personnel/Wenli Zhou/Continue Education/2022-continue education/Multi-Drug Test Cup (Urine) Package Insert AP.pdf
policy_evidence.snippet:
【STORAGE AND STABILITY】
Store as packaged in the sealed pouch at 2-30°C. The test is stable through the expiration date printed
on the sealed pouch. The test Cups must remain in the sealed pouch until use. DO NOT FREEZE. Do
not use beyond the expiration date. 【SPECIMEN COLLECTION AND PREPARATION】
Urine Assay
The urine specimen should be collected in a clean and dry container. Urine collected at any time of the
day may be used. Urine specimens exhibiting visible precipitates should be centrifuged, filtered, or
allowed to settle to obtain a clear specimen for testing. Specimen Storage
Urine specimens may be stored at 2-8°C for up to 48 hours prior to testing. For prolonged storage,
specimens may be frozen and stored below -20°C. Frozen specimens should be thawed and mixed
well before testing. When testing cards with S.V.T. or Alcohol storage of urine specimens should not
exceed 2 hours at room temperature or 4 hours refrigerated prior to testing. 【MATERIALS】 Materials Provided  Test Cups  Package insert
 Adulteration Color Chart (when applicable)
Materials Required But Not Provided
 Specimen collection container  timer 【DIRECTIONS FOR USE】
Allow the test, urine specimen, and/or controls to reach room temperature (15-30ºC)
prior to testing.

checks.gap_analysis: Status: Partial. While the 'C1003.0V3-XYZ Lab Chemical Hygiene Plan' mandates that all chemical containers have a legible, firmly attached label, the provided documentation does not contain specific records (logs or photos) demonstrating that laboratory-prepared reagents, calibrators, or controls are consistently labeled with the required elements (content, quantity/concentration, storage, date prepared, and expiration). The 'G1013.0_Laboratory_Reagent_Policy' addresses storage temperature monitoring but does not explicitly confirm the labeling process for in-house prepared solutions or the use of a traceable log system as permitted by the COM.30300 note. Compliance is not fully verified as no audit logs or physical evidence of labeling practices were provided for review.
corrective_actions: 1) Implement a standardized labeling template or log system that captures all required elements: content, concentration/titer, storage requirements, date prepared/reconstituted, and expiration date.
2) Conduct a retrospective audit of all laboratory-prepared reagents and chemicals to ensure current containers are labeled or traceable to the new log system.
3) Update G1013.0_Laboratory_Reagent_Policy to explicitly define the labeling or log-traceability requirements for all reagents and solutions.
checks.ai_evidence_summary: **COM.30300**: All reagents, calibrators, controls, stains, chemicals, and solutions must be clearly labeled with the reagent name or content, storage temperature or condition, and expiration date on the lot box or primary container. When a new reagent container is opened, laboratory personnel must confirm it is not expired and label it with the open date and expiration date if not already present. If storage conditions or opening the container change the expiration date, the new expiration date and content must be labeled on the tube. Laboratory-prepared reagents, master mixes, or chemical mixes require labels including the reagent name, concentration (if applicable), date prepared, preparer's name, storage condition, and expiration date. The elements of content and quantity, concentration or titer, storage requirements, date prepared, filtered or reconstituted by the laboratory, and expiration date may be recorded in a log traceable to the containers. The C1003.0V3-XYZ Lab Chemical Hygiene Plan also states that all chemical containers shall have a legible, firmly attached label showing the contents and hazard information.

policy_evidence.snippet:
If you are
unsure of how to properly dispose of chemicals/material, contact the safety officer. 7.0 LABELING CHEMICAL CONTAINERS 1. All chemical containers shall have a legible, firmly attached label showing the contents of the container and hazard information. 2. Labels on incoming containers of hazardous chemicals shall not be removed or defaced. 3. SDSs for hazardous chemicals in a given laboratory shall be available to all employees in the
laboratory. 4. If a chemical substance is produced in the laboratory for another use outside of the laboratory,
the SDS and labeling provisions of the OSHA Hazard Communication Standard apply. The lab
manager shall ensure these requirements are met. 5. Chemical substances developed in the laboratory shall be assumed to be hazardous in the
absence of other information. Such chemicals shall be labeled and stored in appropriate
containers. Appropriate PPE shall be worn when handling chemical substances developed in the
laboratory, and an SDS shall be created. 8.0 EXPOSURE MONITORING 1. Employee exposures to any substance regulated by an OSHA standard shall be measured when
there is reason to believe that exposure levels routinely exceed the action levels specified in 29
CFR 1910, Subpart Z. 2. Employee exposures to OSHA regulated substances shall not exceed the permissible exposure
limit (PEL) specified in 29 CFR 1910, Subpart Z. PPE and engineering controls should be used
to prevent employee exposure.

policy_evidence.snippet:
Equipment Calibration Program XYZ Lab Document Name
XYZ Lab Document Number F1002.0 Version # 6 Author： XYZ Lab Date of Inception: 11/02/2020 Start Date of Current Version：04/26/2026 Page 1 of 3 1. Objective
This document is to ensure laboratory instrument/equipment calibration, calibration verification or function check so as to
maintain on-going analytical continuity and accuracy for both quantitative and qualitative test systems. Definition:
1.1 Calibration: calibration is a set of operations that establish, under specified conditions, the relationship between
reagent system/instrument response and the corresponding concentration/activity values of an analyte. 1.2 Calibration verification/function check: calibration verification denotes the process of confirming that the current
calibration settings for each analyte remain valid for a test system. 2. Process and Requirements
2.1 The laboratory must perform equipment/instrument calibration at a defined interval following the manufacturer's
instruction. 2.2 Calibration can be performed by the equipment manufacturer, a certified third-party provider or trained and qualified
laboratory staff. 2.3 The laboratory shall have a calibration log for each equipment/instrument to document the calibration schedule and
result. 2.4 The lab general supervisor or designee shall be in charge of the calibration schedule to ensure all
equipment/instruments are calibrated when it is first placed in service and thereafter on schedule.
policy_evidence.title: F1002.0V6-Equipment Calibration Program

checks.requirement: All reagents (chemicals, stains, controls, media, antibodies, test strips, testing cartridges, etc.) are stored and handled as defined by the laboratory and following the manufacturer's instructions.
checks.subject: Reagent Storage and Handling - Nonwaived Tests
checks.note:
NOTE: Reagents must be stored and handled in a manner that will prevent environmentally-induced alterations that could affect reagent stability and test performance. Prepared reagents must be properly stored, mixed, when appropriate, and discarded when stability parameters are exceeded. 
  
  If the manufacturer defines a required storage temperature range, the temperature of storage areas must be monitored daily. Refer to the Temperature-Dependent Instruments, Equipment, and Environment section of the checklist for requirements for monitoring and recording temperature. 
  
  If the laboratory identifies a problem with a reagent that was used for patient testing (eg, expired vial or reagent subjected to unacceptable storage conditions, etc.), the laboratory must evaluate the potential impact on patient test results and retain records of the evaluation and actions taken.
checks.evidence_of_compliance:
Evidence of Compliance: 
  
  * Records of reagent storage and handling consistent with manufacturer's instructions, including refrigerator, freezer and room temperature monitoring
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Partial. The laboratory has established a robust framework for reagent management through 'G1013.0 Laboratory Reagent Policy' and 'G1008.0V2-PCR Lab Cross Contamination Prevention Program', which define storage, handling, and preparation requirements. Specific manufacturer instructions for storage are documented in 'IFUK.US.MOL2655-02 FLU 2.0.pdf'. However, while the policy exists, the required evidence of compliance—specifically the daily temperature monitoring logs for refrigerators, freezers, and room temperature storage areas—was not verified in the provided documentation. The laboratory must provide these records to demonstrate that the policies are being executed as required by the checklist.
corrective_actions: 1) Implement and maintain daily temperature monitoring logs for all reagent storage units (refrigerators, freezers, and room temperature areas).
2) Ensure all temperature logs are reviewed and signed by the supervisor or designee to verify compliance with manufacturer storage specifications.
3) Retain these logs as evidence of ongoing adherence to G1013.0 Laboratory Reagent Policy.
cited_documents: G1008.0V2-PCR Lab Cross Contamination Prevention Program.pdf
checks.ai_evidence_summary: **COM.30350**: The "Laboratory Reagent Policy" G1013.0_Laboratory_Reagent_Policy outlines requirements for reagent selection, purchasing, receiving, labeling, storage, verification, preparation, usage, monitoring, and disposal to ensure quality, safety, traceability, and reliable patient testing results. All reagents must be stored at the manufacturer's specified temperature and environmental conditions. For example, Simplexa™ Flu A/B & RSV Direct Gen II reagents must be stored at -10 to -30 °C in a non-frost-free freezer and thawed at room temperature (18 to 25 °C) before use. The Reaction Mix should not be vortexed or refrozen. Reagents should also be stored away from light. The "PCR Lab Cross Contamination Prevention Program" G1008.0V2-PCR Lab Cross Contamination Prevention Program specifies that reagents for nucleic acid amplification should be prepared, aliquoted, and stored in a dedicated reagent preparation area. The lot number of stock reagents used for master mix preparation must be documented in the reagent preparation form and recorded in the testing batch record for traceability. Reagents should not be used beyond their expiration dates. Records of reagent storage and handling, including temperature monitoring, were requested but not found in the provided documents.

policy_evidence.document_uri: gs://xyzlapp-inspect-050526/Inspection Documents_2026/Lab Policies/G-Test Process Management/G1008.0V2-PCR Lab Cross Contamination Prevention Program.pdf
policy_evidence.snippet:
2.3 Reagents and Solutions
2.3.1 All reagents used in nucleic acid amplification shall be prepared, aliquoted, and stored in the reagent preparation
area that is separated from the areas used for sample preparation and amplification.
2.3.2 Dedicated equipment and supplies shall be used for reagent preparation. 2.3.3 Master mixes shall be made for specific assays according to a corresponding SOP and if applicable, aliquoted to a
specific volume required for each batch of the test. This practice will minimize the number of times that a single stock
reagent tube is opened so that to reduce the risk for contamination.
2.3.4 The lot number of the stock reagents used for the master mix preparation should be documented in the reagent
preparation form. The lot number will be recorded in the testing batch record that will make easier for source
identification should cross contamination occurs. 2.3.5 When setting up a reaction, reagents (deoxyribonucleoside triphosphates (dNTPs), primers, buffers, and enzymes)
shall always be added prior to adding the sample. When setting up multiple reactions, first make a master mix of reagents
enough for all samples, then aliquot the mix into reaction tubes or wells and add the sample last. It is important to only
open the tube of a reagent or a sample at the point of use and cap it right after.
policy_evidence.title: G1008.0V2-PCR Lab Cross Contamination Prevention Program

policy_evidence.snippet: Simplexa™ Flu A/B & RSV Direct Gen II (MOL2655) — Page 3 RECOMMENDED MATERIALS 1. Universal transport medium (UTM) to use as a No Template Control (NTC). REAGENT HANDLING AND STORAGE 1. Store reagents at -10 to -30 °C (do not use a frost-free freezer). 2. Allow reagents to thaw at room temperature (approximate range 18 to 25 °C) before use. 3. Do not use kits or reagents beyond their expiration dates. 4. After removing Reaction Mix from freezer storage, initiate the test within thirty (30) minutes. 5. Do not vortex the Reaction Mix. 6. Do not refreeze the Reaction Mix. WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS 1. Wear personal protective equipment, such as (but not limited to) gloves and lab coats when handling kit reagents and equipment. Wash hands thoroughly when finished performing the test. 2. Do not pipette by mouth. 3. Do not smoke, drink, eat, handle contact lenses or apply make-up in areas where kit reagents and/or human specimens are being used. 4. Follow your institution’s safety procedures for working with chemicals and handling biological specimens. 5. Do not use reagents beyond their expiration date. 6. Dispose of unused kit reagents and human specimens according to local, state and federal regulations.

To establish standardized requirements for the selection, purchasing, receiving, labeling, storage, verification,
preparation, usage, monitoring, and disposal of laboratory reagents to ensure quality, safety, traceability, and
reliable patient testing results. Control Plan 1. Reagent Selection, Purchase, and Receiving

inventory procedures E1001.0. 1.2 Newly purchased reagents shall be recorded in the laboratory inventory system (XYZTool Inventory Tab)
upon receipt. 1.3 Upon receipt, reagents shall be inspected for correct item and quantity, intact packaging, acceptable shipping
condition, lot number, expiration date, and evidence of temperature excursion if applicable. 1.4 Any damaged, expired, leaking, mislabeled, improperly shipped, or otherwise compromised reagent shall be
quarantined and reported to the laboratory supervisor or designee before use. 2. Reagent Storage and Environmental Control
2.1 All reagents shall be stored at the temperature and environmental conditions required by the manufacturer.

checks.requirement: All reagents (chemicals, stains, controls, media, antibodies, test strips, testing cartridges, etc.) are used within their indicated expiration date.
checks.subject: Reagent Expiration Date - Nonwaived Tests
checks.note:
NOTE: Expiration dates assigned by a manufacturer must be observed. The laboratory must assign an expiration date if an expiration date is not provided by the manufacturer. The laboratory must base the assigned expiration date on known stability, frequency of use, storage conditions, and risk of deterioration. 
  
  Transfusion service laboratories may use rare reagents (ie, rare antisera and selected panel red cells to determine the specificity of red cell antigens and antibodies) beyond their expiration date if appropriate positive and negative controls are run each day of use and react as expected. The laboratory must have in-date reagents for routine antigen typing and antibody panel testing 
  
  For histology and cytology, laboratories may satisfy confirmation of ongoing acceptable performance of stains until the expiration date by technical assessment of case material containing suitable material for evaluation of stains, or by use of suitable control specimens. 
  
  Laboratories not subject to US regulations and military laboratories in overseas locations, may use expired reagents only under the following circumstances: 1) The reagents are unique, rare or difficult to obtain; or 2) Delivery of new shipments of reagents is delayed through causes not under control of the laboratory. The laboratory must retain records of verification of the performance of expired reagents in accordance with written laboratory procedure. The laboratory must also retain records of its efforts to obtain reagents in a timely manner and the rationale for continuing to perform the test instead of referring it to another laboratory. 
  
  Laboratories subject to US regulations must not use expired reagents.

checks.requirement: New reagent lots and shipments are checked against previous reagent lots or with suitable reference material before or concurrently with being placed in service.
checks.subject: New Reagent Lot and Shipment Confirmation of Acceptability - Nonwaived Tests
checks.note:
NOTE: This requirement applies to reagents that provide a chemical or biological reaction to detect and/or measure a target analyte and would not apply to inert ingredients (eg, reagent water, saline) or materials used for specimen preparation. 
  
  The purpose of this check is to confirm that the use of new analytic reagent lots and shipments (including different shipments of the same lot) do not affect patient results. Matrix interferences between different lots of reagents may impact the calibration status of instruments and consistency of patient results. Improper storage conditions during shipping of reagents may have a negative impact on their ability to perform or exhibit the same levels of reactivity as intended. 
  
  The minimum extent of the reagent check is described below; however, the check must be at least as extensive as described in the manufacturer's instructions. The laboratory may determine the number of specimens tested. 
  
  Qualitative: For qualitative nonwaived tests, minimum cross-checking includes retesting at least one positive and negative specimen with known reactivity against the new reagent lot. Utilization of a weakly positive specimen is recommended for confirmation of acceptability. 
  
  Examples of suitable reference materials for qualitative tests include: 
  
  * Positive and negative patient specimens tested on a previous lot; 
  * Previously tested proficiency testing materials; 
  * External QC materials tested on the previous lot (eg, antigen testing kit controls, immunohematology antisera and reagent red cells) 
  * Control strains of organisms or previously identified organisms for microbiology reagents used to detect or evaluate cultured microorganisms; 
  * If there is documentation that none of the above options is available, control material provided by the assay manufacturer with the new test kit. 
  
  There are more specific requirements in other checklists for some types of qualitative testing, such as: 
  
  * Flow cytometry antibodies and reagents (FLO.23325) 
  * Microbiology media and stains, disks/strips, antimicrobials, and reagents (eg, MIC.11038, MIC.21540, MIC.21560, MIC.21624, MIC.21626, MIC.21910, MIC.65320) 
  * Immunohistochemistry antibody and detection system reagents (ANP.22760, CYP.04380, BAP.05363). 
  
  Quantitative: For quantitative nonwaived tests, patient specimens are preferred for comparing a new lot against the previous lot, when possible. Manufactured materials, such as proficiency testing (PT) or QC materials may be affected by matrix interference between different reagent lots, even if results show no change following a reagent lot change. The use of patient specimens confirms the absence of matrix interference. The following materials may be used: 
  
  * Patient specimens tested on a previous lot 
  * Reference materials or QC products provided by the method manufacturer with method specific and reagent lot specific target values 
  * Proficiency testing materials with peer group established means 
  * QC materials with peer group established means based on interlaboratory comparison that is method specific and includes data from at least 10 laboratories 
  * Third-party general purpose reference materials if commutable with patient specimens for the method (per package insert or method manufacturer) 
  * QC material in use with the current reagent lot to check a new shipment of the same reagent lot (There should be no change in potential matrix interactions with use of the same lot number of reagent and QC material). 
  
  For automated analyzers that use reservoirs for testing reagents (eg, many hematology analyzers, some urine analyzers), the laboratory must define the process for checking new lots of reagents. Any manufacturer's instructions must be followed.
checks.evidence_of_compliance:
Evidence of Compliance: 
  
  * Records for the introduction of new lots and shipments, including lot number(s) tested and comparison of results to the acceptability criteria
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Non-Compliant. The laboratory failed to provide evidence of a written procedure or documented records for the verification of new reagent lots and shipments as required by COM.30450. The retrieved documents (e.g., K1003.3.1_Data Collection Form, F1006.2-Emergency Shutdown Procedure) focus on equipment maintenance and general QA data collection but do not address the specific requirement to compare new reagent lots against previous lots or suitable reference materials. There is no evidence of a defined process for checking new shipments or lots to ensure patient results are not impacted by matrix interferences or improper storage conditions. Records for lot number tracking and acceptability criteria comparisons were not verified.
corrective_actions: 1) Develop and implement a written procedure for the verification of new reagent lots and shipments that meets the minimum requirements for qualitative or quantitative testing as specified in COM.30450.
2) Create a standardized log or electronic record system to document the introduction of new lots, including lot numbers, comparison results, and verification of acceptability criteria.
3) Train laboratory staff on the new procedure and ensure all future reagent lot changes are documented according to the updated policy.

checks.evidence_of_compliance:
Evidence of Compliance: 
  
  * Manufacturer's instrument/equipment instructions for each waived test AND 
  * Records of instrument/equipment maintenance and function checks as required by the manufacturer
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Partial. The laboratory has established an Equipment Maintenance Program (F1003.0-Equipment Maintenance Program) and utilizes specific data collection forms (K1003.3.3_Data Collection Form for maintenance and functionality check.docx) to document maintenance and function checks. While the policy requires adherence to manufacturer instructions, the retrieved documents indicate a potential gap in verification. Specifically, the document '2024 K1003.3.3_Data Collection Form for maintenance and functionality check.docx' explicitly questions whether function checks are consistently performed and verified as acceptable prior to patient testing. Although the search summary states that records are reviewed monthly, the actual records of completed maintenance and function checks for waived tests were not provided for audit verification. To achieve full compliance, the laboratory must demonstrate that the documented maintenance and function checks align with the specific manufacturer's instructions for each waived test and confirm that these checks are consistently performed and reviewed prior to reporting patient results.
corrective_actions: 1) Perform a retrospective audit of maintenance and function check logs for all waived tests to ensure they align with manufacturer-specific requirements.
2) Implement a formal sign-off process on the 'Data Collection Form for maintenance and functionality check' to verify that function checks are acceptable before patient testing begins.
3) Ensure all maintenance records are readily available for inspection as per the two-year retention policy.

All instrument users are required to follow these protocols for pre- and post-run maintenance. Maintenance and function checks are performed and recorded, with records kept in the instrument's file folder or shared drive for at least two years. These records are reviewed monthly by the Technical Supervisor. The laboratory also confirms that personnel follow manufacturer's instructions for controls, reagents, and kits, including for waived tests. Any deviations from manufacturer instructions are properly recorded.

checks.requirement: The laboratory verifies the performance of all instruments and equipment prior to initial use, after major maintenance or service, and after relocation to ensure that they run according to expectations.
checks.subject: Instrument/Equipment Performance Verification
checks.note:
NOTE: Instrument/equipment performance verification (NOT to be confused with validation or verification of the test method performance specifications) includes processes to verify that the instruments and equipment perform according to expectations for the intended use and within defined tolerance limits. 
  
  If instruments or equipment are moved, the laboratory must perform appropriate function checks to ensure that they were not adversely affected by the relocation process or changes due to the new environment. This does not apply to portable equipment used following the manufacturer's instructions.
checks.evidence_of_compliance:
Evidence of Compliance: 
  
  * Records of appropriate function checks
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Compliant. The laboratory has established a robust framework for equipment performance verification as required by COM.30550. Policies defined in 0XYZ0001.0Rev3-Quality Manual2025 and F1001.0-Installation Operation and Performance Qualification (3Q) Process.pdf mandate IQ/OQ/PQ for initial use, relocation, and major maintenance. The laboratory utilizes K1003.3.3_Data Collection Form for maintenance and functionality check.docx to document these activities. Furthermore, F1003.0-Equipment Maintenance Program.pdf explicitly addresses relocation requirements, ensuring manufacturer instructions are followed to prevent adverse effects. The system includes a mechanism for labeling equipment as 'Unverified - DO NOT USE' until performance verification is successfully completed and reviewed by quality management.
corrective_actions: Continue current practice of performing and documenting IQ/OQ/PQ for all new, relocated, or repaired equipment using the K1003.3.3_Data Collection Form.
cited_documents: F1001.0-Installation Operation and Performance Qualification (3Q) Process.pdf
K1003.3.3_Data Collection Form for maintenance and functionality check.docx
checks.ai_evidence_summary: **COM.30550**: XYZ Lab maintains equipment performance through installation (IQ), operational (OQ), and performance (PQ) qualifications. IQ follows manual instructions, while OQ and PQ occur upon installation, relocation, repair, or at defined intervals. Failed qualifications require removal from service, deviation documentation, and manufacturer intervention. Calibration and verification follow manufacturer instructions at set intervals, with verification required after major repairs or failed quality control. Failed verifications trigger an investigation, corrective action, and re-verification before returning to service. All activities are documented and reviewed by quality management. Equipment relocation requires adherence to safe handling instructions and validation per F1001.0-Installation Operation and Performance Qualification （3Q）Process and F1002.0V6-Equipment Calibration Program. Equipment must be labeled "Unverified - DO NOT USE" until verification is complete.

policy_evidence.snippet:
2.9 The laboratory should have an appropriate thermometric standard device of known accuracy, which is certified to
meet NIST standards or traceable to NIST standards. 2.9.1 Thermometric standard devices must be recalibrated, recertified, or replaced prior to the date of expiration of the
guarantee of calibration or they are subject to requirements for non-certified thermometers.
2.9.2 All non-certified thermometers should be verified using a certified calibrated thermometer annually. 2.9.3 Thermometers without defined expiration dates must be treated as non-certified thermometers after two years
from the certificate date. 2.9.4 Thermometers should be periodically evaluated for damage (eg, separation of columns). Thermometers with
obvious damage must be rechecked before continued use. 2.10 The temperature for all temperature sensitive instruments/equipment shall be monitored at use and thermometers
be calibrated at least annually. 2.11 For centrifuges used to separate different components, the speed shall be tested and calibrated at least once every
year. 2.12 The calibration and calibration verification procedure for micropipettor is as follows： The accuracy and precision of a newly purchased pipettor shall be verified before the manufacture calibration is due. There is no need for recalibration if verification passes. The accuracy and precision of old pipettors shall be verified once every six months.If the verification passes, there
is no need for re-calibration.

Purpose This policy provides direction for laboratory processes and procedures to select, install,
maintain, and calibrate equipment and for how service and problems are recorded to
ensure that equipment performs as intended from acquisition to decommission. Selection and
acquisition Equipment is provided and replaced as needed to ensure the quality of laboratory services. The laboratory selects equipment by identifying the necessary functional specifications
and the facility, environmental, and engineering requirements needed for providing
services. Acquisition and purchasing is done in collaboration with XYZ Laboratory’s
purchasing/contracting resource functions. Equipment
identification
and
qualifications Each instrument and piece of equipment is uniquely identified, and a master list of
laboratory equipment is maintained. Installation qualification is performed according to the operator’s manual setup
instructions, including both pre-performance approval of the installation plan and post
performance approval and follow-up of results. Operational qualification confirms the equipment is operational for its intended use and
locations, including both pre-performance approval of the operational plan and post
performance approval and follow-up of results. Performance qualification (including examination method verification and validations, as
appropriate) is performed by laboratory personnel to ensure that, through documented
processes and procedures, instruments and equipment perform as intended, including
both pre-performance approval of the performance plan and post-performance approval
and follow-up of results.

checks.requirement: Written procedures for start-up, operation, maintenance, and shutdown of instruments and equipment, as applicable, are available in a paper-based, electronic, or web-based format at the workbench or in the work area.
checks.subject: Instrument/Equipment Operation
checks.note: NOTE: The procedures must include steps to perform an emergency shutdown and handling of workload during instrument downtime, as applicable. These may be separate approved procedures or be included in the testing procedure for a specific analyte.
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Partial. While the Quality Manual (0XYZ0001.0Rev3-Quality Manual2025) and the Instrument/Equipment Standard Operating Protocol Guide (F1007.0V2) establish the framework for equipment management, the current documentation lacks evidence that specific, individual instrument SOPs contain the mandatory emergency shutdown and workload handling procedures required by the COM.30575 note. The search summary indicates that Form F1006.2 is intended to capture these procedures, but this form was not provided for review. Furthermore, while training records (D1003.1_Lab Instrument and Equipment Training Record) confirm personnel are trained on emergency procedures, the actual written procedures at the workbench for specific instruments were not verified as complete against the requirement for emergency shutdown and downtime contingency planning.
corrective_actions: 1) Audit all individual instrument/equipment SOPs to ensure they explicitly include emergency shutdown steps and workload handling procedures during downtime.
2) Ensure that the finalized procedures, including Form F1006.2, are physically or electronically accessible at the specific workbench or work area for each instrument.
cited_documents: D1003.1_Lab Instrument and Equipment Training Record
checks.ai_evidence_summary: **COM.30575**: All electronic or special non-electronic equipment must have a written instrument/equipment SOP. This SOP should include clear instructions for turning on and shutting down the equipment in both normal and emergency situations (Form F1006.2). It must also detail maintenance procedures, calibration frequency and method, performance checks, troubleshooting procedures, and manufacturer repair contact information. Purpose This policy provides direction for laboratory processes and procedures to select, install,
maintain, and calibrate equipment and for how service and problems are recorded to
ensure that equipment performs as intended from acquisition to decommission. Selection and
acquisition Equipment is provided and replaced as needed to ensure the quality of laboratory services. The laboratory selects equipment by identifying the necessary functional specifications
and the facility, environmental, and engineering requirements needed for providing
services. Acquisition and purchasing is done in collaboration with XYZ Laboratory’s
purchasing/contracting resource functions. Equipment
identification
and
qualifications Each instrument and piece of equipment is uniquely identified, and a master list of
laboratory equipment is maintained. Installation qualification is performed according to the operator’s manual setup

locations, including both pre-performance approval of the operational plan and post
performance approval and follow-up of results. Performance qualification (including examination method verification and validations, as
appropriate) is performed by laboratory personnel to ensure that, through documented
processes and procedures, instruments and equipment perform as intended, including
both pre-performance approval of the performance plan and post-performance approval
and follow-up of results.

checks.gap_analysis: Status: Compliant. checks.ai_evidence_summary: **COM.30580**: The laboratory monitors environmental conditions daily to ensure optimal test system performance. This includes checking and recording storage conditions like temperature and humidity in the "XYZ Lab Temperature and Humidity Record". The acceptable temperature and humidity ranges are listed in the Conditional References tab of this record and at the top of the daily monitoring log. These ranges are determined based on the reagents and instruments stored in the area, compared to temperature standards. If temperature or humidity falls outside the acceptable range, the laboratory director is alerted, and troubleshooting occurs to identify the root cause and implement a solution. Corrective action is taken, and affected supplies, reagents, or samples are checked for accuracy or quality before use. A dehumidifier is present in Room 310 to maintain optimal humidity for instruments and reagents. All thermometers are calibrated annually against a NIST traceable thermometer.

checks.requirement: The laboratory performs and records appropriate maintenance and function checks for all instruments (eg, analyzers) and equipment (eg, centrifuges) following a defined schedule, at least as frequently as specified by the manufacturer.
checks.subject: Maintenance/Function Checks
checks.note:
NOTE: Maintenance and function checks may include (but are not limited to) cleaning, electronic, mechanical and operational checks. 
  
  The purpose of a function check is to detect drift, instability, or malfunction, before the problem is allowed to affect test results. 
  
  For equipment without manufacturer's instructions defining maintenance and function check requirements, the laboratory must establish a schedule and procedure that reasonably reflects the workload and operating specifications of its equipment. 
  
  It is up to the laboratory to determine how and where records of maintenance checks are recorded. Equipment not in use does not require maintenance or function checks, but these checks must be performed before putting the equipment back into service.
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Non-Compliant. While the laboratory maintains an IQCP program (IQCP Quality Assessment_202402.docx) and job descriptions (D1001.5V3), there is no evidence of a master maintenance schedule or completed maintenance/function check logs for laboratory equipment. The search summary confirms that while IQCP assessments were performed, the specific records required by COM.30600—demonstrating that maintenance is performed at least as frequently as manufacturer specifications—were not provided. The retrieved documents include a Cloud User Manual and OSHA regulations, but neither constitutes the required laboratory-specific maintenance logs or a defined schedule for equipment such as centrifuges or analyzers. The laboratory must establish and document a schedule for all equipment and provide evidence of completed checks.
corrective_actions: 1) Develop a comprehensive master maintenance and function check schedule for all laboratory equipment, ensuring frequencies meet or exceed manufacturer specifications.
2) Implement a standardized log system to record all maintenance and function checks, ensuring these are reviewed and signed off by the laboratory director or designee at least monthly.
3) Retain all completed maintenance records for inspection to demonstrate compliance with the established schedule.

checks.requirement: The laboratory takes and records corrective action when tolerance limits for acceptable function of instruments and equipment are exceeded.
checks.subject: Function Check Tolerance Limits
checks.note:
NOTE: The defined tolerance limits must follow the manufacturer's specified limits. Function checks must be within the defined tolerance limits prior to use for testing patient samples. 
  
  The action related to tests that have an approved Individualized Quality Control Plan (IQCP) must include an assessment of whether further evaluation of the risk assessment and quality control plan is needed based on problems identified (eg, trending for repeat failures, etc.).
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Partial. The laboratory has established policies for corrective action regarding equipment function checks, including temperature/humidity monitoring (C1001.0V2-Laboratory Facility Routine Maintenance Program.pdf, 0XYZ0001.0Rev3-Quality Manual2025.pdf) and IQCP-specific failures (XYZ-MOL-Micro-IQCP-Simplexa.docx). While the policy framework is documented, the current evidence set lacks specific, completed corrective action records (e.g., logs showing a failure, the subsequent investigation, and the documented resolution) to verify that these policies are consistently implemented in practice. The laboratory must demonstrate that when tolerance limits are exceeded, the required documentation of the investigation and corrective action is consistently recorded and reviewed.
corrective_actions: 1) Compile a representative sample of completed corrective action logs for equipment function check failures to demonstrate adherence to policy.
2) Ensure all corrective action documentation includes the required assessment of risk and potential impact on patient samples as per the IQCP requirements.
checks.ai_evidence_summary: **COM.30625**: The laboratory has established procedures for taking corrective action when instrument and equipment function checks exceed tolerance limits. For instance, if calibration verification fails, the affected equipment is taken offline, an investigation is performed to identify the root cause, corrective action is taken, and new calibration verification is performed before the equipment is returned to service. Similarly, if temperatures or humidity are out of range for fridges, freezers, and incubators, an investigation and corrective action are performed. The Quality Manual also states that if temperatures exceed acceptable levels, appropriate corrective action will be taken, and affected supplies, reagents, or samples will be checked for accuracy or quality before use. For pipettors, if verification does not pass, the pipettor must not be used and needs to be sent for calibration and repair if necessary. The XYZ-MOL-Micro-IQCP-Simplexa document outlines that corrective action and revision of the Quality Control Plan (QCP) are required when unexpected QC failures or unacceptable Proficiency Testing results occur, or when equipment maintenance/monitoring logs indicate issues.

policy_evidence.snippet:
2.9 The laboratory should have an appropriate thermometric standard device of known accuracy, which is certified to
meet NIST standards or traceable to NIST standards. 2.9.1 Thermometric standard devices must be recalibrated, recertified, or replaced prior to the date of expiration of the
guarantee of calibration or they are subject to requirements for non-certified thermometers.
2.9.2 All non-certified thermometers should be verified using a certified calibrated thermometer annually. 2.9.3 Thermometers without defined expiration dates must be treated as non-certified thermometers after two years
from the certificate date. 2.9.4 Thermometers should be periodically evaluated for damage (eg, separation of columns). Thermometers with
obvious damage must be rechecked before continued use. 2.10 The temperature for all temperature sensitive instruments/equipment shall be monitored at use and thermometers
be calibrated at least annually. 2.11 For centrifuges used to separate different components, the speed shall be tested and calibrated at least once every
year. 2.12 The calibration and calibration verification procedure for micropipettor is as follows： The accuracy and precision of a newly purchased pipettor shall be verified before the manufacture calibration is due. There is no need for recalibration if verification passes. The accuracy and precision of old pipettors shall be verified once every six months.If the verification passes, there
is no need for re-calibration.

policy_evidence.document_uri: gs://xyzlapp-inspect-050526/Inspection Documents_2026/Lab Policies/C-Laboratory Safety/C1001.0V2-Laboratory Facility Routine Maintenance Program.pdf
policy_evidence.snippet:
Fridges, freezers, and incubators shall also be
recorded daily. If the temperature or humidity is out of range, investigation and corrective action shall be performed. 2.6 The laboratory should have an emergency power supply system that meets lab equipment power needs. 2.7 Prevention of Electrical Hazards
Laboratory environment contains potential electrical hazards including electric shock and electrocutions caused by faulty
electrical equipment/instrumentation or wiring; damaged receptacles and connectors; and unsafe work practices. The
laboratory is committed to meet the following requirements to eliminate the potential electrical hazards at its work place:
a. All equipment/instruments must be installed and used according to manufacturer's instructions. b. All instruments must be grounded. c. Sufficient access and working space must be provided and maintained around all electrical equipment to permit
ready and safe operation and maintenance of such equipment. d. Power cord plugs on equipment shall be checked frequently to assure that it is firmly connected to the power
outlet, with none of the contacts exposed. e. Extension cords and gang plugs are prohibited for large instruments. f. Remove all damaged receptacles and portable electrical equipment from service. g. Repair all damaged receptacles and portable electrical equipment before placing them back into service. h. Ensure all workers are trained not to plug or unplug energized equipment when their hands are wet. i.

policy_evidence.snippet:
COM.04250
If the laboratory uses more than one nonwaived instrument/method to test for a given
analyte, the instruments and methods are checked against each other at least twice
a year for comparability of results. NOTE: This requirement applies to tests performed on the same or different instrument makes/
models or by different methods, even if there are different reference intervals or levels of
sensitivity. It includes primary and back up methods used for patient testing. The purpose of the requirement is to evaluate the relationship between test results using different
methodologies, instruments, or testing sites. The laboratory must establish a written procedure for
this check that includes acceptance criteria. This requirement is not applicable to: Calculated parameters Waived methods Laboratories with different CAP numbers
The following types of materials may be used to generate data for comparability studies: Patient/client specimens (pooled or unpooled) are preferred to avoid potential matrix effects Quality control materials for tests performed on the same instrument platform, with both control materials
and reagents of the same manufacturer and lot number. Alternative protocols based on quality control or reference materials for cases when availability or pre
analytical stability of patient/client specimens is a limiting factor. The materials must be validated (when
applicable) to have the same response as fresh human specimens for the instruments and methods
involved.

COM.04250
If the laboratory uses more than one nonwaived instrument/method to test for a given
analyte, the instruments and methods are checked against each other at least twice
a year for comparability of results. NOTE: This requirement applies to tests performed on the same or different instrument makes/
models or by different methods, even if there are different reference intervals or levels of
sensitivity. It includes primary and back up methods used for patient testing. The purpose of the requirement is to evaluate the relationship between test results using different
methodologies, instruments, or testing sites. The laboratory must establish a written procedure for
this check that includes acceptance criteria. This requirement is not applicable to: Calculated parameters Waived methods Laboratories with different CAP numbers
The following types of materials may be used to generate data for comparability studies: Patient/client specimens (pooled or unpooled) are preferred to avoid potential matrix effects Quality control materials for tests performed on the same instrument platform, with both control materials
and reagents of the same manufacturer and lot number. Alternative protocols based on quality control or reference materials for cases when availability or pre
analytical stability of patient/client specimens is a limiting factor. The materials must be validated (when
applicable) to have the same response as fresh human specimens for the instruments and methods
involved.

This program is to ensure when a problem arises, the laboratory instrument/equipment can be inspected and repaired in a

pre-selected reference laboratory for processing until the instruments are fixed and verified for meeting expected
specifications.

Equipment Calibration Program XYZ Lab Document Name
XYZ Lab Document Number F1002.0 Version # 6 Author： XYZ Lab Date of Inception: 11/02/2020 Start Date of Current Version：04/26/2026 Page 1 of 3 1. Objective
This document is to ensure laboratory instrument/equipment calibration, calibration verification or function check so as to
maintain on-going analytical continuity and accuracy for both quantitative and qualitative test systems. Definition:
1.1 Calibration: calibration is a set of operations that establish, under specified conditions, the relationship between
reagent system/instrument response and the corresponding concentration/activity values of an analyte. 1.2 Calibration verification/function check: calibration verification denotes the process of confirming that the current
calibration settings for each analyte remain valid for a test system. 2. Process and Requirements
2.1 The laboratory must perform equipment/instrument calibration at a defined interval following the manufacturer's
instruction. 2.2 Calibration can be performed by the equipment manufacturer, a certified third-party provider or trained and qualified
laboratory staff. 2.3 The laboratory shall have a calibration log for each equipment/instrument to document the calibration schedule and
result. 2.4 The lab general supervisor or designee shall be in charge of the calibration schedule to ensure all
equipment/instruments are calibrated when it is first placed in service and thereafter on schedule.

a new expiration date must be recorded if opening the container changes the expiration date, storage

Equipment Calibration Program XYZ Lab Document Name
XYZ Lab Document Number F1002.0 Version # 6 Author： XYZ Lab Date of Inception: 11/02/2020 Start Date of Current Version：04/26/2026 Page 1 of 3 1. Objective
This document is to ensure laboratory instrument/equipment calibration, calibration verification or function check so as to
maintain on-going analytical continuity and accuracy for both quantitative and qualitative test systems. Definition:
1.1 Calibration: calibration is a set of operations that establish, under specified conditions, the relationship between
reagent system/instrument response and the corresponding concentration/activity values of an analyte. 1.2 Calibration verification/function check: calibration verification denotes the process of confirming that the current
calibration settings for each analyte remain valid for a test system. 2. Process and Requirements
2.1 The laboratory must perform equipment/instrument calibration at a defined interval following the manufacturer's
instruction. 2.2 Calibration can be performed by the equipment manufacturer, a certified third-party provider or trained and qualified
laboratory staff. 2.3 The laboratory shall have a calibration log for each equipment/instrument to document the calibration schedule and
result. 2.4 The lab general supervisor or designee shall be in charge of the calibration schedule to ensure all
equipment/instruments are calibrated when it is first placed in service and thereafter on schedule.
