checks.ai_evidence_summary: **DRA.10430**: The Laboratory Director Qualification and Responsibility document, D1001.1V3-Lab Director Job Description and Responsibility, outlines the laboratory director's qualifications and responsibilities for a high complexity laboratory. The director is responsible for the overall operation of the laboratory, overseeing personnel employment, ensuring duties are performed per regulations, and developing a quality system approach for accurate testing. Non-delegated responsibilities include ensuring all laboratory services are appropriate for the patient population, adequate laboratory conditions, a safe employee environment, and sufficient, appropriately educated personnel. The director also ensures documentation is completed for procedure manuals, proficiency testing results, and monthly QA/QC monitors, and that employee responsibilities are in writing. The External Accreditation Management Process document, K1001.0-External Accreditation Management Process, indicates the laboratory participates in CAP accreditation and undergoes biennial onsite inspections and annual self-inspections. The self-inspection process involves the lab director or technical supervisor training the inspection team, evaluating documents and records, identifying deficiencies, developing corrective actions, and monitoring their implementation. The director is also responsible for ensuring a clear understanding of laboratory operations and effective monitoring of improvement measures.

checks.requirement: For laboratories subject to US regulations, on-site laboratory director visits occur at least every six months (with at least four months between the two on-site visits).
checks.subject: Director On-Site Visits - Laboratories Subject to US Regulations
checks.note:
NOTE: This requirement applies when the laboratory director is not routinely on site. On-site visits must, at minimum, occur at the frequency described above. More frequent visits may be defined based on input from the medical staff and administration, and upon the complexity and volume of testing. 
  
  The requirement for on-site visits pertains to only one location site visit per CLIA certificate. The laboratory director may determine which site needs to be included during each on-site visit. 
  
  Records of on-site visits must include evidence that activities were performed that are part of the laboratory director responsibilities (eg, assessment of physical environmental conditions and adequacy of staffing).
checks.evidence_of_compliance:
Evidence of Compliance: 
  
  * Records of laboratory director activities for on-site visits AND 
  * Records for frequency of on-site visits AND 
  * Document defining frequency for on-site visits
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Non-Compliant. The laboratory failed to provide documentation verifying that the laboratory director conducts on-site visits at least every six months with a minimum four-month interval between visits. Per the search_summary, onsite verification is required but currently lacks documentation. The laboratory has not provided a policy defining the frequency of these visits, nor have they produced records of director activities (e.g., assessment of physical environmental conditions or staffing adequacy) as required by the Evidence of Compliance criteria. No corrective actions or onsite notes were provided to indicate that these visits have occurred or that a schedule has been established.
corrective_actions: 1) Establish and document a formal policy defining the frequency of laboratory director on-site visits in accordance with CLIA requirements.
2) Implement a standardized log or report template to record the date of each on-site visit and the specific director activities performed during the visit.
3) Ensure the schedule maintains at least a four-month interval between visits and a maximum of six months between visits.
checks.ai_evidence_summary: [NON-COMPLIANT]: Onsite verification required but not documented.

checks.requirement: For laboratories not subject to US regulations, on-site laboratory director visits occur at least once per year.
checks.subject: Director On-Site Visits - Laboratories Not Subject to US Regulations
checks.note:
NOTE: This requirement applies when the laboratory director is not routinely on site. On-site visits must, at minimum, occur at the frequency described above. More frequent visits may be defined based on input from the medical staff and administration, and based upon the complexity and volume of testing. 
  
  The requirement for on-site visits pertains to only one location site visit per CAP-accredited laboratory. The laboratory director may determine which site needs to be included during each on-site visit. 
  
  Records of on-site visits must include evidence that activities were performed that are part of the laboratory director responsibilities (eg, assessment of physical environmental conditions and adequacy of staffing).
checks.evidence_of_compliance:
Evidence of Compliance: 
  
  * Records of laboratory director activities for on-site visits AND 
  * Records for frequency for on-site visits AND 
  * Document defining frequency for on-site visits
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Non-Compliant. The laboratory failed to provide documentation of on-site visits by the laboratory director as required for laboratories not subject to US regulations. Per the search summary, onsite verification is required but currently lacks documentation. The laboratory has not provided a policy defining the frequency of visits, nor have records been produced demonstrating that the director performed required activities such as assessing physical environmental conditions or staffing adequacy during an on-site visit within the past 12 months.
corrective_actions: 1) Establish and document a formal policy defining the frequency of on-site laboratory director visits (minimum once per year).
2) Implement a standardized log or report template to record director activities performed during on-site visits, including environmental and staffing assessments.
3) Schedule and conduct an on-site visit and maintain the resulting documentation for future inspection.
checks.ai_evidence_summary: [NON-COMPLIANT]: Onsite verification required but not documented.

checks.requirement: The involvement of the laboratory director, including activities performed on-site and through remote consultation, is considered adequate by the laboratory administration, medical staff, and the inspection team, and follows written policy or agreement.
checks.subject: Director Involvement
checks.evidence_of_compliance:
Evidence of Compliance: 
  
  * Records of laboratory director activities (on-site and remote) AND 
  * Meeting minutes showing director participation AND 
  * Laboratory director review of quality management records AND 
  * Evidence of availability for consultations with medical staff as appropriate (based on interview with medical and laboratory staff or records of consultations)
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Non-Compliant. While the laboratory has established policies defining the Laboratory Director's responsibilities (D1001.1V3-Lab Director Job Description and Responsibility.pdf), there is no documented evidence of the Director's active involvement in laboratory operations. The current documentation lacks records of Director activities (on-site or remote), meeting minutes demonstrating participation, evidence of quality management record reviews, or proof of availability for medical staff consultations. The requirement mandates that the Director ensure effective communication mechanisms and maintain records of these interactions; these records were not verified during the document review. The missing evidence category 'onsite' remains unaddressed as no logs or sign-in records were provided to substantiate physical presence or active oversight.
corrective_actions: 1) Establish and maintain a log of Laboratory Director activities, including on-site visits, remote consultations, and participation in quality management meetings.
2) Implement a formal communication record system to document consultations with medical staff and laboratory management regarding test results and quality issues.
3) Conduct a retrospective review of quality management records and ensure the Laboratory Director signs or initials these documents to provide evidence of oversight.
cited_documents: D1001.1V3-Lab Director Job Description and Responsibility.pdf
checks.ai_evidence_summary: **DRA.10435**: The laboratory director oversees operations, including personnel management, regulatory compliance, and quality system development, while retaining non-delegable duties such as ensuring appropriate patient services, adequate testing conditions, and employee safety. The director must ensure the presence of a General Supervisor and maintain documentation for the Procedure Manual, Proficiency Testing, and QA/QC monitors. While the director assumes Clinical Consultant duties, they may delegate medical consultations and report requirements to a Clinical Consultant, and assign the production of quality assessment materials and Proficiency Testing reviews to a Technical Supervisor. The Technical Supervisor provides scientific oversight, while the General Supervisor reports to the director or technical leadership. Despite these defined roles, the retrieved documents lack records of director activities, meeting minutes, evidence of quality management reviews, or proof of availability for medical staff consultations.

checks.requirement: The laboratory director ensures an effective QMS for the laboratory.
checks.subject: Effective Quality Management System (QMS)
checks.note: NOTE: The laboratory director must be involved in the design, implementation and oversight of the laboratory's QMS as set forth in GEN.13806.
checks.evidence_of_compliance:
Evidence of Compliance: 
  
  * Written QMS covering all areas of the laboratory AND 
  * Records of laboratory director approval of the QMS and the selection of quality indicators AND 
  * Records (eg, reports, QMS meeting minutes) of laboratory director review of quality indicators, annual assessment of QMS, complaints, and incidents with development and implementation of plans of corrective and preventive action (when taken)
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Partial. The laboratory has established a foundational QMS framework, including the 'Quality Management Review Process' (A1003.0) and the 'Annual Laboratory QMS Implementation Assessment Form' (K1003.8). The 'Lab Director Job Description' (D1001.1V3) outlines the director's responsibility for the QMS. However, while the policy framework is present, the current evidence lacks specific, dated records demonstrating the laboratory director's active, documented approval of the current Quality Manual (0XYZ0001.0Rev3) and the specific selection of quality indicators. Furthermore, while an annual assessment was performed on 4/27/2025 (K1003.8), the provided documentation does not include the required meeting minutes or reports showing the director's review of complaints, incidents, and the subsequent implementation of corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) as mandated by the Evidence of Compliance criteria.
corrective_actions: 1) Obtain and archive documented evidence of the Laboratory Director's formal approval of the current Quality Manual (0XYZ0001.0Rev3) and the selection of quality indicators.
2) Compile and maintain a record of periodic QMS review meeting minutes that explicitly document the Director's review of complaints, incidents, and the status of CAPA activities.

K1003.8_Annual Laboratory QMS Implementation Assessment Form.docx
checks.ai_evidence_summary: **DRA.10440**: The laboratory director and organizational quality manager are responsible for establishing and implementing a Quality Management System (QMS) program in compliance with regulatory requirements and accreditation criteria. The QMS outlines the framework for monitoring processes, identifying problems, improving processes, and ensuring quality in services. The laboratory director is responsible for the overall operation of the laboratory and ensures the effective application of the QMS, with all personnel trained on its content and processes. The director also approves new technical policies and procedures, as well as substantial changes to existing documents. Laboratory management periodically reviews QMS data and information, quality goals, and objectives to ensure ongoing suitability and effectiveness. An "Annual Laboratory QMS Implementation Assessment Form" is used to evaluate the effectiveness of the QMS, including performance of quality indicators and corrective and preventive actions. The Quality Management Review Process (A1003.0) establishes a quality management team, led by the lab director, to review the QMS at planned intervals. The lab director or designee reviews QA and QC documents, such as batch records and corrective action reports, prior to issuing test reports.

policy_evidence.snippet:
While each department XYZ Laboratory has obligations to comply with policies and procedures that ensure
to deliver high quality services to patients and clients, laboratory director and organization quality manager
endorsed by CEO is responsible for establishing and implementing a QMS program in compliance with
regulatory requirements and accreditation criteria. QMS outlines the framework in which the Lab continually monitors its processes, identifies problems,
improves processes, and ensures quality is built into the services provided. Implementing a QMS enhances
the opportunity to deliver consistent, high-quality, and cost-effective tests, products, and services. The QMS model describes the management foundation of quality building blocks (ie, the quality system
essentials [QSEs]) and demonstrates how the foundation supports the laboratory’s path of workflow as
depicted in Figure 1.

checks.subject: Director Responsibility - Interim Self-inspection
checks.note:
NOTE: CAP-accredited laboratories are required to complete an interim self-inspection, using the CAP checklists, at the start of the second year of the laboratory's two-year accreditation cycle, unless an exception is granted by the CAP. It is an important aspect of continuing education, laboratory improvement, and continuous compliance. The use of a variety of mechanisms for self-inspection (residents, technologists or others trained to perform inspections) is strongly endorsed. Self-inspection by personnel familiar with, but not directly involved in, the routine operation of the laboratory section to be inspected is recommended.

Policy K1003.0V2 (Internal Assessment and Audit Program) provides the procedural foundation for collecting evidence, evaluating findings, and verifying corrective actions. checks.requirement: The laboratory director ensures that proficiency testing, alternative performance assessment, and QC procedures are sufficient for the extent of testing performed in the laboratory.
checks.subject: Director Responsibility - PT/QC
checks.evidence_of_compliance:
Evidence of Compliance: 
  
  * Records of PT and alternative performance assessment data, investigation, and corrective action, as applicable AND 
  * Written QC procedures for all areas of the laboratory AND 
  * Records of laboratory director or designee review of QC and corrective actions AND 
  * Records of laboratory director or designee involvement when PT/QC problems directly affect patient care
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Partial. The laboratory has established clear policy documentation regarding the Laboratory Director's and Technical Supervisor's responsibilities for PT and QC oversight, as evidenced by D1001.1V3, D1001.2V2, and 5-D1001.2. These documents define the delegation of duties for performance verification and QC monitoring. However, the current evidence set lacks the required records of actual implementation. Specifically, while the search summary confirms the director's responsibility for reviewing PT reports and QC data, the actual records of director or designee review of QC, investigation of PT/alternative performance assessment results, and documentation of corrective actions were not provided for verification. To achieve full compliance, the laboratory must produce the specific logs or signed reports demonstrating that these oversight activities are occurring as described in the job descriptions.
corrective_actions: 1) Compile and maintain a centralized file of signed Laboratory Director or designee reviews for monthly QC and PT/alternative performance assessment reports.
2) Implement a standardized corrective action log for all 'unacceptable' PT or QC results, ensuring each entry includes the Director's signature or documented involvement.

checks.ai_evidence_summary: **DRA.10460**: The laboratory director is responsible for ensuring and supervising the development and maintenance of quality assessment and quality control programs. This includes overseeing enrollment in CMS-Approved proficiency testing and ensuring PT samples are tested and reviewed by appropriate staff. The director also delegates to a Technical Supervisor the review of performance on Proficiency Testing results, including recommendations on corrective actions and documentation. Furthermore, the director ensures that remedial actions are documented and systems for maintenance are identified by keeping appropriate documentation on test systems. The director also delegates to the General Supervisor and/or Lab Manager the observation and review of monthly QC, with notification to the Lab Director if there are any issues. Records of ongoing review of all PT reports and alternative performance assessment results by the laboratory director or designee are required. Records of investigation of each "unacceptable" PT and alternative performance assessment result, including corrective action, are also necessary.

checks.requirement: The laboratory director ensures that the performance specifications for new tests, instruments, and methods introduced to the laboratory have been properly validated or verified prior to being used for patient testing.
checks.subject: Director Responsibility - New Method Validation/Verification
checks.note:
NOTE: Specific requirements are in the All Common Checklist (Instruments & Equipment, Test Method Validation/Verification, and Method Performance Specifications sections) and in other checklists. 
  
  Artificial intelligence and machine learning algorithms implemented by the laboratory for patient testing are subject to this requirement.
checks.evidence_of_compliance:
Evidence of Compliance: 
  
  * Written procedures for validation/verification studies AND 
  * Records of new method validation/verification approval and supporting data
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Partial. The laboratory has established a framework for compliance through 'G1004.0V3-Test Validation and Verification Program.pdf', which mandates the inclusion of all instruments in validation studies, and 'K1003.3.5_Data Collection Form for Verification of performance Specification.docx', which provides a template for data collection. Additionally, 'A1002.0V2-Quality Planning Process.pdf' outlines the overarching quality planning structure. However, while the policy and data collection tools are present, the current evidence set lacks specific, completed records of Laboratory Director approval for recent validation/verification studies. To meet the requirement, the laboratory must provide documented evidence that the Director has reviewed and signed off on the validation reports and supporting data for new methods or instruments prior to patient testing implementation.
corrective_actions: 1) Compile and maintain a central file of completed validation/verification reports for all active methods/instruments.
2) Ensure each report includes a formal signature/approval by the Laboratory Director as required by DRA.10475.
3) Conduct a retrospective audit of recent method implementations to ensure all Director approvals are documented.
cited_documents: K1003.3.5_Data Collection Form for Verification of performance Specification.docx
checks.ai_evidence_summary: **DRA.10475**: The laboratory director is responsible for ensuring that new tests, instruments, and methods are properly validated or verified before patient testing. This includes documenting the validation or verification process and results, which must be reviewed and approved by the lab director. A validation plan, approved by the lab director, is required before initiating validation experiments. The validation report, detailing the experiments and any deviations, must also be approved by the lab director. For any analyte with multiple testing methods or platforms, the alternative method's performance must be verified every six months using split samples, with results documented and reviewed by the lab director or designee. The laboratory must also have written SOPs for sample collection, labeling, transportation, receiving, and processing to ensure sample quality and integrity.

checks.requirement: The laboratory director ensures communication of laboratory data and appropriate result reporting.
checks.subject: Director Responsibility - Communication
checks.evidence_of_compliance:
Evidence of Compliance: 
  
  * Records of oversight of computer services and changes AND 
  * Evidence that test reports have been reviewed within the medical record OR 
  * Lab communications, newsletters, etc.
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Non-Compliant. The laboratory has failed to provide the required evidence to demonstrate the Director's oversight of communication regarding laboratory data and result reporting. While '7-D1001.1V2-Lab Director Job Description and Responsibility.pdf' outlines the Director's general responsibilities, it does not provide the specific records required by the checklist. Specifically, there is no evidence of oversight of computer services and changes, no documentation of test report reviews within medical records, and no examples of laboratory communications or newsletters. The 'Test Requisition Form 2023' confirms the lab's policy to defer interpretation to physicians, but this does not satisfy the requirement for the Director to ensure the communication of laboratory data and reporting processes. No records were verified to support the active oversight of these communication channels.
corrective_actions: 1) Establish and maintain a log or meeting minutes documenting the Director's oversight of computer services, system changes, and laboratory reporting updates.
2) Implement a periodic audit process to verify that test reports are appropriately reviewed within the medical record and maintain these audit logs as evidence.
3) Initiate a formal laboratory communication process (e.g., newsletters or memos) to inform clinical staff of laboratory data updates and reporting changes.
checks.ai_evidence_summary: **DRA.10500**: The Laboratory Director is responsible for communicating local, state, and federal regulations, as well as company policy to employees. The Director or their designee must review SOPs at least every two years to ensure they are current and meet user requirements. The Director also ensures that test result reports include pertinent information for specific patient interpretation. While the Director can delegate responsibilities such as providing consultations to physicians regarding laboratory findings, and overseeing personnel performance, the provided documents do not contain records of oversight of computer services and changes, evidence of test reports reviewed within the medical record, or lab communications/newsletters. The Test Requisition Form 2023 indicates that patients understand it is their responsibility to discuss results with a physician and that the laboratory will not provide interpretation or consultation.

Laboratory Chemical Hygiene Plan (LCHP) XYZ Lab Document Name
XYZ Lab Document Number C1003.0 Version # 3 Author: XYZ Lab Date of Composition：11/14/2020 Date of Execution：04/25/2026 XYZ Laboratory 2009 Ranch Rd. 620 N. STE 325, Austin, TX 78734 Page 3 of 28 Laboratory Standard without fear of retribution. 4.2 Responsibilities
Laboratory Director -- The Laboratory Director (or their appointee) shall: 1. Be responsible for helping communicate local, state, and federal regulations, as well as company
policy to employees. 2. Develop a laboratory-specific CHP (LCHP) for their laboratory. 3. Perform Laboratory Safety Assessment and prepare laboratory-specific SOP’s for all hazardous
laboratory operations that reflect appropriate safety practices and precautions. 4. Review and update the LCHP at least annually and any time a new piece of equipment or process
is added to the laboratory. 5. Investigate accidents/near-accidents, and document these incidents. With the goal of improving
laboratory safety in mind, encourage employees to report accidents/near-accidents and make
improvements to equipment or procedures accordingly. Laboratory safety officer 1. Ensure the laboratory safety policy is current and meet the national and international standards 2. Working with the local government safety regulatory agency to ensure compliance of the
laboratory operation 3. Provide safety train for all laboratory employee

2.1 Written Policy and standard operating procedures (SOPs): the laboratory shall have written policy and SOP
for every step of the patient sample testing process from sample receiving to reporting as well as for the general
laboratory operations. The SOPs shall be approved by the laboratory director before use. Laboratory director or
its designee shall review SOPs at least once every two years to ensure the procedures are up to date and meet
the requirements of the users. 2.2 Specimen identification and integrity: all specimens shall be identified and labeled (refer to G1001.0 and
GS1001. 0) to ensure accuracy throughout the testing process. 2.3 Complaints Investigation and resolution: all complaints and problems reported to the laboratory shall be
documented, investigated. When necessary, corrective actions shall be taken to resolve the problem. Complaints, investigation process and corresponding corrective actions shall be documented with an
Investigation and Improvement Report Form (refer to B1003.0 and B1003. 1) and monitored for improvement. 2.4 Communications: the laboratory shall document problems that occur as result of breakdowns in
communication between the laboratory and the customers （refer to B1003.0 and B1003.1）. Corrective action
must be taken to resolve the problem and prevent any future occurrence.

policy to employees. 2. Develop a laboratory-specific CHP (LCHP) for their laboratory. 3. Perform Laboratory Safety Assessment and prepare laboratory-specific SOP’s for all hazardous

laboratory safety in mind, encourage employees to report accidents/near-accidents and make

results.snippet:
2.1 Written Policy and standard operating procedures (SOPs): the laboratory shall have written policy and SOP
for every step of the patient sample testing process from sample receiving to reporting as well as for the general
laboratory operations. The SOPs shall be approved by the laboratory director before use. Laboratory director or
its designee shall review SOPs at least once every two years to ensure the procedures are up to date and meet
the requirements of the users. 2.2 Specimen identification and integrity: all specimens shall be identified and labeled (refer to G1001.0 and
GS1001. 0) to ensure accuracy throughout the testing process. 2.3 Complaints Investigation and resolution: all complaints and problems reported to the laboratory shall be
documented, investigated. When necessary, corrective actions shall be taken to resolve the problem. Complaints, investigation process and corresponding corrective actions shall be documented with an
Investigation and Improvement Report Form (refer to B1003.0 and B1003. 1) and monitored for improvement. 2.4 Communications: the laboratory shall document problems that occur as result of breakdowns in
communication between the laboratory and the customers （refer to B1003.0 and B1003.1）. Corrective action
must be taken to resolve the problem and prevent any future occurrence.

checks.requirement: The laboratory director provides for intralaboratory consultations and clinical consultations regarding the ordering of appropriate tests and the medical significance of laboratory data.
checks.subject: Director Responsibility - Consultations
checks.note:
NOTE: Only physicians or doctoral scientists may provide clinical consultations. 
  
  The laboratory director must be accessible to the laboratory for on-site, telephone, or electronic consultations, as needed, or ensure that a qualified designee is available in the director's absence.
checks.evidence_of_compliance:
Evidence of Compliance: 
  
  * Policy or call schedule for the availability of the laboratory director and designee(s) to provide consultations AND 
  * Policy or statement signed by the laboratory director authorizing individuals responsible for clinical consultations AND 
  * Records of laboratory director or designee involvement for the ordering of tests and/or interpretation of results AND 
  * Evidence of the availability of the laboratory director or designee for consultative services (based on interview with medical staff or records)
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Non-Compliant. While the laboratory has established job descriptions for the Laboratory Director (D1001.1V3) and Clinical Consultant (D1001.3V3), the documentation is insufficient to meet the requirements of DRA.10700. Specifically, the laboratory lacks a formal policy or call schedule defining the availability of the Director or designee for consultations. Furthermore, there is no evidence of a signed statement by the Laboratory Director explicitly authorizing individuals responsible for clinical consultations. Finally, no records were provided to demonstrate actual involvement of the Director or designee in test ordering consultations or the interpretation of laboratory data, nor was there evidence of availability for consultative services as required by the checklist.
corrective_actions: 1) Develop and implement a formal policy or call schedule detailing the availability of the Laboratory Director and designated Clinical Consultants for consultations.
2) Create a signed authorization document from the Laboratory Director formally delegating clinical consultation responsibilities to qualified personnel.
3) Establish a log or record-keeping system to document all instances of clinical consultations, including test ordering guidance and interpretation of results.
cited_documents: D1001.1V3-Lab Director Job Description and Responsibility.pdf
D1001.3V3-Clinical Consultant Job Description and Responsibility.pdf
checks.ai_evidence_summary: **DRA.10700**: The Laboratory Director delegates responsibilities for clinical consultations to a Clinical Consultant. These delegated duties include providing consultations to physicians regarding the medical significance of laboratory findings, assisting clients in ordering appropriate tests, and ensuring test reports contain pertinent information for patient interpretation. The Clinical Consultant is also responsible for ensuring consultation availability and communication to clients regarding test result quality and interpretation for specific patient conditions. The Clinical Consultant's qualifications require either a licensed physician or a doctoral degree in a relevant science with specific experience. The Laboratory Director, Wenli Zhou, explicitly states in 7-D1001.1V2-Lab Director Job Description and Responsibility that they assume the responsibilities of the Clinical Consultant, including availability for consultation and ensuring test reports include pertinent information. No separate policy or call schedule for the availability of the laboratory director and designee(s) for consultations was found. Records of laboratory director or designee involvement for ordering tests and/or interpretation of results, and evidence of availability for consultative services (based on interview with medical staff or records) were not found.

policy_evidence.snippet:
Clinical Consultant Qualification and Responsibility Document Name
Document Number： D1001.3 Version # 3 Author：Wenli Zhou Date of Composition: 11/01/2020 Date of Execution：04/24/2026 Page 1 of 2 1. Objective
Provide the qualification and responsibilities of the laboratory Clinical Consultant of a high complexity molecular
diagnostic laboratory 2. Qualifications
2.1 An MD, DO, DPM licensed to practice medicine in the jurisdiction where the laboratory is located (if
required) or. 2.2 A doctoral degree in a chemical, biological, clinical or medical laboratory science, or medical technology
from an accredited institution, certified by an HHS-approved board, and For high complexity testing, at least two years of laboratory training or experience, or both, and
experience supervising high complexity testing;. Or For moderate complexity testing, at least one year of experience directing or supervising nonwaived
laboratory testing. 3. Job Relations
Interact with Lab Director, Technical Supervisors, General Supervisor, Scientists, Technicians, other testing
personnel, and customers. 4. Job Summary
The Clinical Consultant is to provide consultation regarding the appropriateness of the testing ordered and
interpretation of test results. 5. Job Duties and Responsibilities
5.1 Available to provide clinical consultation to the laboratory’s clients. 5.2 Assists the laboratory’s clients in ensuring that appropriate tests are ordered to meet clinical expectations.

checks.requirement: The laboratory director ensures sufficient numbers of personnel with appropriate educational qualifications, documented training and experience, and adequate competency to meet the needs of the laboratory.
checks.subject: Director Responsibility - Personnel
checks.note:
NOTE: For laboratories subject to US regulations, all personnel must meet the personnel requirements of CLIA or other US equivalent regulations (eg, Clinical Laboratory Improvement Program Procedures for Department of Defense laboratories, Veterans Health Administration Handbook 1106.01). For laboratories not subject to US regulations, all personnel requirements must be defined and met. 
  
  While the laboratory director must ensure provisions of appropriately trained supervisory and testing personnel, the laboratory director may delegate (in writing) many of the duties relating to hiring, training, and supervising personnel to other qualified designees. 
  
  Staffing should be considered insufficient if there is clear evidence from quality monitoring records, data derived from complaints or concerns, turnaround time, error statistics, etc.
checks.evidence_of_compliance:
Evidence of Compliance: 
  
  * Records indicating that personnel meet requirements for the level of testing (complexity) performed and delegated tasks are performed AND 
  * Records of training, competency assessment, and continuing education in personnel files AND 
  * Records of periodic on-site assessment of the adequacy of staffing by the laboratory director
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Partial. The laboratory has established policies defining personnel qualifications and director responsibilities as evidenced by D1001.1V3 and D1001.5V3. These documents confirm the director's role in overseeing employment and ensuring appropriate staffing levels. However, the current evidence set lacks the required records of periodic on-site assessment of the adequacy of staffing by the laboratory director, as well as specific records of training, competency assessment, and continuing education for current staff. While job descriptions are in place, the actual performance records required by the 'Evidence of Compliance' section were not verified.
corrective_actions: 1) Compile and maintain a central file containing documented evidence of periodic on-site staffing adequacy assessments performed by the laboratory director.
2) Ensure all personnel files contain current, signed records of training, competency assessments, and continuing education as required by the Evidence of Compliance criteria.

checks.ai_evidence_summary: **DRA.11300**: The laboratory director is responsible for the overall operation of the laboratory. This includes overseeing the employment of personnel and ensuring that a sufficient number of appropriately educated personnel are employed. The director must also ensure that all duties are performed per regulations and that sufficient numbers of appropriately trained supervisory and technical staff are employed, with their responsibilities identified. The qualifications for personnel performing high complexity testing are detailed in D1001.5V3-Test personnel job description and responsibilities and 5-D1001.5V2-Test personnel job description and responsibilities-CW, requiring a minimum of a Bachelor's degree in a relevant science or equivalent training and experience. For moderate complexity testing, personnel must qualify as high complexity testing personnel or have an Associate degree in a relevant science or nursing, or a high school diploma with specific military training or equivalent experience. The director also oversees laboratory personnel performance and competency and plans for training or continuing education needs.

checks.note: NOTE: The laboratory director must ensure compliance with OSHA and national, federal, state (or provincial), and local laws and regulations, as well as other applicable safety regulations. Details may be found in the Laboratory Safety and Specimen Transport and Tracking sections of the Laboratory General Checklist. Additional safety requirements may also be found in the discipline-specific checklists (eg, Microbiology Checklist, Anatomic Pathology Checklist).
checks.evidence_of_compliance:
Evidence of Compliance: 
  
  * Safety policies and procedures AND 
  
  * Records of safe work practice reviews with corrective action taken to correct violations AND 
  * Safety meeting minutes AND 
  * Chemical hygiene plan AND 
  * Records of periodic on-site assessment of physical and environmental conditions by the laboratory director
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Partial. The laboratory has established foundational safety documentation, including the 'C1003.0V3-XYZ Lab Chemical Hygiene Plan' and the 'K1003.5_Annual Laboratory, Regulatory, and Safety Compliance Check' (dated 07/11/2025). While the annual walk-around record confirms the director's periodic assessment of physical conditions, the current evidence set lacks documentation for safety meeting minutes and records of specific safe work practice reviews with associated corrective actions. The existing documentation satisfies the requirement for a Chemical Hygiene Plan and periodic on-site assessment, but the absence of meeting minutes and specific violation/corrective action logs prevents full compliance with the 'Evidence of Compliance' criteria.
corrective_actions: 1) Establish and maintain a formal log of safety meeting minutes to document ongoing staff communication regarding safety protocols.
2) Implement a tracking system for safe work practice reviews that includes documentation of identified violations and subsequent corrective actions taken.

checks.ai_evidence_summary: **DRA.11400**: The laboratory director ensures a safe environment and regulatory compliance by communicating all applicable policies and regulations to staff. The director must develop, annually review, and update the laboratory-specific Chemical Hygiene Plan (C1003.0V3-XYZ Lab Chemical Hygiene Plan), which governs chemical exposure prevention, personal habits, and housekeeping. Furthermore, the director is responsible for preparing standard operating procedures for hazardous operations and conducting safety assessments. Compliance is verified through the Annual Laboratory, Regulatory, and Safety Compliance Check (K1003.5_Annual Laboratory, Regulatory, and Safety Compliance Check), which documents an annual walk-around to confirm OSHA standards, including the maintenance of fire extinguishers, evacuation routes, eyewash stations, electrical grounding, and sharps management. Finally, the director oversees the availability of MSDS sheets, adherence to local chemical waste disposal procedures, and the documentation of annual safety training.

policy_evidence.snippet:
COM.01700
There is ongoing evaluation of proficiency testing (PT) and alternative performance
assessment results with appropriate corrective action taken for each unacceptable
result. NOTE: Each unacceptable PT or alternative performance assessment result (any result or sample
not meeting defined acceptability criteria) must be evaluated. It is recommended that the
laboratory investigate acceptable results that show significant bias or trends. Primary records related to PT and alternative performance assessment testing are retained for
at least two years (five years for transfusion medicine). These include all instrument tapes, work
cards, computer printouts, evaluation reports, evidence of review, and records of follow-up or corrective
action. For laboratories outside the US, PT failures relating to problems with shipping and specimen stability should
include working with local customs and health regulators to ensure appropriate transit of PT specimens
Evidence of Compliance:
3 Records of ongoing review of all PT reports and alternative performance assessment results by the
laboratory director or designee AND
3 Records of investigation of each “unacceptable” PT and alternative performance assessment result
including records of corrective action appropriate to the nature and magnitude of the problem

policy_evidence.snippet:
Laboratory Chemical Hygiene Plan (LCHP) XYZ Lab Document Name
XYZ Lab Document Number C1003.0 Version # 3 Author: XYZ Lab Date of Composition：11/14/2020 Date of Execution：04/25/2026 XYZ Laboratory 2009 Ranch Rd. 620 N. STE 325, Austin, TX 78734 Page 3 of 28 Laboratory Standard without fear of retribution. 4.2 Responsibilities
Laboratory Director -- The Laboratory Director (or their appointee) shall: 1. Be responsible for helping communicate local, state, and federal regulations, as well as company
policy to employees. 2. Develop a laboratory-specific CHP (LCHP) for their laboratory. 3. Perform Laboratory Safety Assessment and prepare laboratory-specific SOP’s for all hazardous
laboratory operations that reflect appropriate safety practices and precautions. 4. Review and update the LCHP at least annually and any time a new piece of equipment or process
is added to the laboratory. 5. Investigate accidents/near-accidents, and document these incidents. With the goal of improving
laboratory safety in mind, encourage employees to report accidents/near-accidents and make
improvements to equipment or procedures accordingly. Laboratory safety officer 1. Ensure the laboratory safety policy is current and meet the national and international standards 2. Working with the local government safety regulatory agency to ensure compliance of the
laboratory operation 3. Provide safety train for all laboratory employee
policy_evidence.title: C1003.0V3-XYZ Lab Chemical Hygiene Plan

policy_evidence.snippet:
(g) Seeks ways to improve the chemical hygiene program. 2. DEPARTMENT CHAIRPERSON OR DIRECTOR (a) Assumes responsibility for personnel engaged in the laboratory use of hazardous chemicals. (b) Provides the chemical hygiene officer (CHO) with the support necessary to implement and maintain the CHP. (c) After receipt of laboratory inspection report from the CHO, meets with laboratory supervisors to discuss cited
violations and to ensure timely actions to protect trained laboratory personnel and facilities and to ensure that the
department remains in compliance with all applicable federal, state, university, local and departmental codes and
regulations. (d) Provides budgetary arrangements to ensure the health and safety of the departmental personnel, visitors, and students. 3. Departmental Safety Committee reviews accident reports and makes appropriate recommendations to the
department chairperson regarding proposed changes in the laboratory procedures. 4. Laboratory Supervisor or Principal Investigator has overall responsibility for chemical hygiene in the laboratory,
including responsibility to:
(a) Ensure that laboratory personnel comply with the departmental CHP and do not operate equipment or handle
hazardous chemicals without proper training and authorization. (b) Always wear personal protective equipment (PPE) that is compatible to the degree of hazard of the chemical. (c) Follow all pertinent safety rules when working in the laboratory to set an example.

checks.requirement: If specific laboratory director functions listed in the NOTE (below) are delegated, the delegation is in writing (by name or job title) and the director ensures that the functions are properly performed by a qualified individual.
checks.subject: Director Responsibility - Documenting Delegation of Specific Functions
checks.note:
NOTE: 
  
  1. This documentation requirement applies to the following specific functions: 
  
  * Review of QC data 
  * Proficiency testing performance 
  * Competency assessment 
  * Test methodology performance studies. 
  
  2. Functions that may not be delegated include the following: 
  
  * Provision of appropriately trained supervisory and technical staff and the identification of their responsibilities 
  * Personal on-site assessment of physical and environmental conditions and the adequacy of staffing on a periodic basis, as defined in written policy 
  * Approval of new technical policies and procedures, as well as substantial changes to existing documents (except as defined in COM.10250 for laboratories not subject to US regulations) 
  * Approval of individualized quality control plans (IQCP). 
  
  3. For the functions listed above that are not personally performed by the laboratory director, the director delegates those tasks to qualified individuals. The responsibilities and duties of supervisors, consultants, and testing personnel performing these functions must be documented in writing by name or job title (eg, job descriptions). Although documentation of delegation is required for the functions listed, activities that are not listed may be performed by others without specific documentation of delegation (eg, temperature recording, function checks, etc.). 
  4. If a delegated function listed above is not being properly performed by the designee and there is no evidence of corrective action, the team leader should cite this requirement as a deficiency, in addition to the specific checklist requirement(s) that relates to the duty not performed (eg, monthly QC review, approval of method validation/verification studies). 
  5. These delegated functions may not be sub-delegated to others by a designee except as specifically outlined in other requirements (eg, GEN.53400, GEN.53600).
checks.evidence_of_compliance:
Evidence of Compliance: 
  
  * Personnel roster accurately indicates qualified individuals performing the above-listed functions AND 
  * Policy or statement signed by the laboratory director authorizing individuals by name or job title to perform tasks on behalf of the laboratory director AND 
  
  * Records showing that delegated tasks are performed by designee, as required
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Partial. The laboratory has established a written delegation policy via 'D1001.1V3-Lab Director Job Description and Responsibility', which explicitly delegates specific functions (QC review, PT performance) to the Technical Supervisor and General Supervisor. The documentation identifies these roles by job title as required. However, while the policy and job descriptions are present, the current evidence set lacks specific records demonstrating that these delegated tasks are being performed by the designees (e.g., signed QC review logs, PT performance reports signed by the designee). Compliance with DRA.11425 requires both the written delegation and evidence that the delegated tasks are actively performed by the qualified individuals. Verification of these performance records is required to achieve full compliance.
corrective_actions: 1) Compile and maintain a representative sample of records (e.g., monthly QC review logs, PT performance reports) signed by the designated Technical or General Supervisor to demonstrate active performance of delegated duties.
2) Ensure all future performance records for delegated functions include the signature or initials of the authorized designee.

checks.ai_evidence_summary: **DRA.11425**: The Laboratory Director Qualification and Responsibility document, D1001.1V3-Lab Director Job Description and Responsibility, and 7-D1001.1V2-Lab Director Job Description and Responsibility outlines the qualifications and responsibilities of the laboratory director for a high complexity laboratory. The director delegates specific responsibilities to a Technical Supervisor, Clinical Consultant, and General Supervisor/Lab Manager. For instance, the Technical Supervisor is delegated the review of proficiency testing results and recommendations for corrective actions, while the General Supervisor and/or Lab Manager are delegated the observation and review of monthly QC. The document also specifies non-delegated responsibilities, such as ensuring a sufficient number of appropriately trained supervisory and technical staff are employed, and the approval of new technical policies and procedures. The document 7-D1001.1V2-Lab Director Job Description and Responsibility includes a signature line for the Laboratory Director, Wenli Zhou, PhD, HCLD, and an attestation that the employee has read, understood, and accepted the requirements.

policy_evidence.document_uri: gs://xyzlapp-inspect-050526/Inspection Documents_2026/Lab Operation/D-Personnel/Wenli Zhou/Job Qualification and Reponsibilites/7-D1001.1V2-Lab Director Job Description and Responsibility.pdf
policy_evidence.snippet:
Laboratory Director Qualification and Responsibility Document Name
Document Number： D1001.1 Version #： 2 Author：Wenli Zhou Date of Composition: 11/01/2020 Date of Execution：01/20/2025 Page 1 of 4 1. Objective
Provide the qualification and responsibilities of laboratory director for the high complexity laboratory 2. Qualifications
2.1 MD, DO, or DPM licensed to practice in the jurisdiction where the laboratory is located (if required), and: 1) Certification in anatomic or clinical pathology, or both, by the American Board of Pathology or American
Osteopathic Board of Pathology, or 2) Have at least two years of experience supervising high complexity testing; and have at least 20 CE credit hours
in laboratory practice that cover director responsibilities as defined below. or 2.2 Doctoral degree (PhD or DPH) in a chemical, biological, or clinical laboratory science from an accredited
institution, and: 1) Have current certification by a board approved by HHS, and 2) Have at least two years of laboratory training or experience or both, and laboratory experience directing or
supervising high complexity testing and 3) Have at least 20 CE credit hours in laboratory practice that cover the director responsibilities defined in the
DRA checklist ( This does not apply to existing laboratory directors that have remained continuously employed in
their current role since December 28, 2024).
policy_evidence.title: 7-D1001.1V2-Lab Director Job Description and Responsibility

policy_evidence.snippet:
PHMSA | PIPELINE AND HAZARDOUS MATERIALS SAFETY ADMINISTRATION 15 OTHER REQUIREMENTS
CARRIAGE BY AIRCRAFT
Section 175.630 contains special requirements for Division 6.1 (poisonous)
materials and Division 6.2 (infectious substances) materials. Paragraph
(c) requires the inspection of each package, overpack, pallet, or unit load
device containing a 6.2 material for signs of leakage. If evidence of leakage
is found, the cargo compartment hold where the 6.2 material was stowed
is required to be disinfected by any means that makes the release of the
6.2 material ineffective at transmitting disease. INCIDENT REPORTING
You must report any release of an infectious substance (Category A or B)
in any mode of transportation to the Department of Transportation. See
§171.15 for telephone reporting requirements and §171.16 for written
report requirements. TRAINING REQUIREMENTS
Employees involved in the packaging and transport of infectious
substances are subject to the training requirements of the HMR. These
requirements vary but are found in §172.704 and include: General awareness/familiarization training; Function-specific training; Safety training; Security awareness training; and In-depth security training (if subject to security plan requirements). Employees involved in the packaging and transport of Category B
infectious substances are required to be trained on the requirements in
§173.199.

checks.requirement: The laboratory director or designee is directly involved in the selection of all laboratory equipment, supplies, and services with respect to quality.
checks.subject: Director Responsibility - Equipment/Services
checks.note: NOTE: The intent is to ensure that the laboratory director has appropriate control over the process. The fact that economic issues are a major factor in these selections does not relieve the laboratory director of responsibility for ensuring the quality of the technical, clinical and operational aspects of the laboratory. The director must ensure that reagents, fluids, parts, materials, and other items supplied to the laboratory meet the requirements for use with instruments and equipment.
checks.evidence_of_compliance:
Evidence of Compliance: 
  
  * Meeting minutes indicating the laboratory director or designee's presence when purchases are discussed OR 
  * Written approval from the laboratory director or designee to purchase equipment
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Partial. The laboratory has established robust policies defining the Director's role in equipment and service selection, specifically through 'E1003.0-Purchasing Process.pdf', 'E1001.0-Supplier Selection Process.pdf', and the '0XYZ0001.0Rev3-Quality Manual2025.pdf'. These documents clearly delegate authority and define quality criteria for procurement. However, while the policy framework is compliant, the current evidence set lacks specific records (e.g., meeting minutes or signed purchase approval forms) demonstrating the Director's active participation in recent equipment or service selections. To achieve full compliance, the laboratory must provide documented evidence of the Director's or their designee's involvement in the actual selection process for recent purchases, as required by the Evidence of Compliance criteria.
corrective_actions: 1) Maintain a log or file of purchase requisitions or equipment selection reports signed by the Laboratory Director or designee.
2) Ensure meeting minutes where equipment or service selection is discussed explicitly document the Director's presence and input.
checks.ai_evidence_summary: **DRA.11475**: The Laboratory Director is responsible for identifying products and capital for order, prioritizing, justifying, selecting, and approving capital purchases. They also provide input into business plans for equipment purchases, rentals, or leases. The Quality Manual states that referral laboratories are selected under the laboratory director’s leadership. The Supplier Selection Process document, E1001.0-Supplier Selection Process, which is approved by the Laboratory Director, provides guidance for evaluating, selecting, and purchasing external services, equipment, reagents, and consumable supplies to ensure quality. This document outlines criteria for equipment selection, including quality products from certified manufacturers, ease of maintenance and calibration, ease of operation, budget adherence, and timely delivery. The laboratory director or designee is also expected to monitor the turnaround time and quality of test results from referral laboratories. The Quality Manual further specifies that roles for purchasing are defined and documented, and a list of selected and approved suppliers is maintained.

checks.requirement: Following a change in laboratory directorship, the new laboratory director approves the technical policies and procedures within three months of the change of directorship (see NOTE).
checks.subject: New Director Policy and Procedure Approval
checks.note:
NOTE: 
  
  1. The approval of the policies and procedures must be recorded. 
  2. The format of such documentation is at the discretion of the laboratory director. It must include an itemization of the documents reviewed and approved, signatures and dates, and demonstrate that all technical policies and procedures have been approved. 
  3. The approval must be completed within three months of the change of directorship for most laboratories. For larger, more complex laboratories where additional time is needed, the laboratory can record an explanation and a schedule for completion of the approvals by the laboratory director. The inspector will verify completion of the approval process for compliance with the schedule. 
  4. Different requirements for approval of new and substantially changed technical policies and procedures and for routine reviews (at least every two years) appear in the All Common Checklist.
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Non-Compliant. While the retrieved documents (D1002.0V3 and D1001.1V3) demonstrate ongoing biennial review and approval of individual policies by the Laboratory Director, there is no evidence of a specific, documented transition process following a change in directorship. The requirement mandates that a new laboratory director must approve all technical policies and procedures within three months of assuming the role. The provided documentation shows routine biennial reviews but lacks an itemized record or formal sign-off demonstrating that the entire technical policy manual was reviewed and approved specifically in the context of a change in directorship. Without a record of this comprehensive transition approval, the laboratory cannot demonstrate compliance with the three-month requirement following a change in leadership.
corrective_actions: 1) Identify the date of the most recent change in laboratory directorship.
2) Conduct and document a comprehensive review of all technical policies and procedures by the current Laboratory Director.
3) Create a formal record (e.g., a signed and dated index or memo) itemizing the reviewed documents to satisfy the three-month transition requirement.

checks.requirement: The laboratory director or designee reviews all technical policies and procedures at least every two years.
checks.subject: Policy and Procedure Review
checks.note:
NOTE: The laboratory director must ensure that the collection of testing policies and technical procedures is complete, current, and has been thoroughly reviewed by a knowledgeable person. Technical approaches must be scientifically valid and clinically relevant. 
  
  To minimize the burden on the laboratory and reviewer(s), the CAP suggests using a schedule whereby roughly 1/24 of all technical policies and procedures are reviewed monthly. Paper/electronic signature review must be at the level of each procedure, or as multiple signatures on a listing of named procedures. A single signature on a Title Page or Index is not a sufficient record that each policy or procedure has been carefully reviewed. Signature or initials on each page of a policy or procedure is not required. 
  
  The laboratory may record review of electronic procedures by: 
  
  * Including statements such as
checks.evidence_of_compliance:
Evidence of Compliance: 
  
  * Records of policy or procedure review
checks.remediation: The biennial review is on the last page of each individual SOPs, and the review for policy is also on the last page of each policy
checks.action_completion: The biennial review is on the last page of each individual SOPs, and the review for policy is also on the last page of each policy
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Compliant. The laboratory has established a process for the biennial review of technical policies and procedures. Per the action_completion note, the laboratory confirms that the biennial review is documented on the last page of each individual SOP and policy. This aligns with the requirement that review must occur at the level of each procedure rather than a single signature on a title page or index. The documentation process described satisfies the criteria for ensuring policies are current and reviewed by a knowledgeable person as outlined in the search_summary.
corrective_actions: Continue current practice of documenting biennial reviews on the final page of each individual policy and SOP to ensure compliance with COM.10100.
checks.ai_evidence_summary: **COM.10100**: The laboratory director or designee is responsible for reviewing all technical policies and procedures at least every two years. This review ensures that the collection of testing policies and technical procedures is complete, current, and has been thoroughly reviewed by a knowledgeable person, confirming scientific validity and clinical relevance. Standard operating procedures (GS series), excluding instrument maintenance procedures (FS series), are specifically noted for biennial review. Policies are also reviewed when the relevant CAP checklist is revised or established. The review process requires paper or electronic signature at the level of each procedure, or multiple signatures on a listing of named procedures, as a single signature on a title page or index is insufficient. Records of review for electronic procedures can be maintained by including statements such as "reviewed by [name of reviewer] on [date of review]" within the electronic record, or by using paper review sheets.

checks.ai_evidence_summary: **COM.04300**: When a laboratory uses multiple nonwaived instruments or methods for the same analyte, they must be checked for comparability at least twice a year. This includes primary and backup methods. The laboratory must have a written procedure for this check, including acceptance criteria. Comparability studies can use patient specimens (preferred), quality control materials, or validated alternative protocols. The requirement applies when instruments/reagents produce the same reportable result. For microbiology, it applies when two instruments detect the same analyte. The "Data Collection Form for Comparison of Test Results" is used to gather data for a QA review, which should then be attached to an Analytic Phase Quality Assessment Review Form. This form asks if secondary/backup instruments or methods are compared to the primary method twice per year for both normal and abnormal values. It also asks if corrective measures were taken when significant deviation was found. One completed form, 2024 K1003.3.7 Data Collection Form for Comparison of Test Results, indicates that there were no backup instruments used during the October 2023 – September 2024 period, but backup assays for the same analytes exist.

policy_evidence.snippet:
COM.04250
If the laboratory uses more than one nonwaived instrument/method to test for a given
analyte, the instruments and methods are checked against each other at least twice
a year for comparability of results. NOTE: This requirement applies to tests performed on the same or different instrument makes/
models or by different methods, even if there are different reference intervals or levels of
sensitivity. It includes primary and back up methods used for patient testing. The purpose of the requirement is to evaluate the relationship between test results using different
methodologies, instruments, or testing sites. The laboratory must establish a written procedure for
this check that includes acceptance criteria. This requirement is not applicable to: Calculated parameters Waived methods Laboratories with different CAP numbers
The following types of materials may be used to generate data for comparability studies: Patient/client specimens (pooled or unpooled) are preferred to avoid potential matrix effects Quality control materials for tests performed on the same instrument platform, with both control materials
and reagents of the same manufacturer and lot number. Alternative protocols based on quality control or reference materials for cases when availability or pre
analytical stability of patient/client specimens is a limiting factor. The materials must be validated (when
applicable) to have the same response as fresh human specimens for the instruments and methods
involved.

1.3.2.1 Accuracy: Accuracy can be assessed using well-characterized reference material together with appropriate
biological matrix or by comparison to another valid test method, such as through specimen exchange， and expressed as
percentage of concordance. For quantitative tests, a minimum of 20 samples with analyte concentrations distributed across
the analytical measurement range should be used. Proportionate mixtures of samples may be used to supplement the study
population. For qualitative tests, a minimum of 20 samples, including positive, negative, and low-positive samples with
concentrations near the lower level of detection should be used; equivocal samples should not be used. For certain
methods that test multiple analytes (eg, next-generation sequencing, FISH, HPLC, GC-MS, MALDI-TOF, etc.), analytic
accuracy may be established for each method (not necessarily each analyte), as appropriate.

checks.gap_analysis: Status: Non-Compliant. The laboratory lacks documented policies or procedures explicitly requiring that organisms in proficiency testing (PT) specimens be identified to the same level as patient samples. While 'XYZ-MOL-Micro-IQCP-Simplexa.docx' acknowledges PT as a risk factor and notes that records are filed, it does not define the analytical scope or identification criteria for PT versus patient testing. No evidence was retrieved confirming that the laboratory's standard operating procedures mandate equivalent identification levels for PT specimens. Consequently, the laboratory cannot demonstrate compliance with the requirement to match patient sample identification depth during PT events.
corrective_actions: 1) Develop and implement a written policy requiring that all PT specimens be processed and identified to the same taxonomic level as routine patient samples.
2) Update the Laboratory Testing Process Control Plan (G1001.0V3) to include specific instructions for PT specimen handling and reporting requirements.
3) Conduct a retrospective review of recent PT reports to ensure identification levels met the required standard and document findings.
checks.ai_evidence_summary: **MIC.00350**: The provided documents do not contain specific policies or procedures regarding the identification level of organisms in proficiency testing specimens compared to patient samples. Therefore, it cannot be verified whether organisms in proficiency testing specimens are identified to the same level as those from patient samples. However, the "Laboratory Testing Process Control Plan" G1001.0V3-Laboratory Testing Process Control Plan_2025 outlines general sample handling, storage, and labeling requirements for patient/customer samples. The "XYZ-MOL-Micro-IQCP-Simplexa" document mentions "Proficiency Testing" as a risk factor with an "Unlikely" frequency of error occurrence and "Negligible" severity of harm to the patient, resulting in an "Acceptable" risk level. It also states that "Proficiency testing records [are] filed in PT folder" and that "No proficiency test was performed in this period". The document further indicates that all trained technologists passed competency during an assessment period and that personnel rotate and review proficiency testing results.

CULTURE An infectious substance containing a pathogen that is intentionally  propagated. Culture does not include a human or animal patient  specimen as defined below. PATIENT SPECIMEN Human or animal materials collected directly from humans or animals  and transported for research, diagnosis, investigational activities, or  disease treatment or prevention. Patient specimen includes excreta,  secreta, blood and its components, tissue and tissue swabs, body parts,  and specimens in transport media (e.g., transwabs, culture media, and  blood culture bottles). REGULATED MEDICAL WASTE Regulated medical waste or clinical waste or (bio) medical waste  means a waste or reusable material derived from the medical treatment  of an animal or human, which includes diagnosis and immunization, or  from biomedical research, which includes the production and testing of  biological products. Regulated medical waste or clinical waste or (bio)  medical waste containing a Category A infectious substance must be  classed as an infectious substance, and assigned to UN2814 or UN2900.

PATIENT SPECIMEN Human or animal materials collected directly from humans or animals  and transported for research, diagnosis, investigational activities, or  disease treatment or prevention. Patient specimen includes excreta,  secreta, blood and its components, tissue and tissue swabs, body parts,  and specimens in transport media (e.g., transwabs, culture media, and  blood culture bottles). REGULATED MEDICAL WASTE Regulated medical waste or clinical waste or (bio) medical waste  means a waste or reusable material derived from the medical treatment  of an animal or human, which includes diagnosis and immunization, or  from biomedical research, which includes the production and testing of  biological products. Regulated medical waste or clinical waste or (bio)  medical waste containing a Category A infectious substance must be  classed as an infectious substance, and assigned to UN2814 or UN2900.

results.snippet:
COM.04250
If the laboratory uses more than one nonwaived instrument/method to test for a given
analyte, the instruments and methods are checked against each other at least twice
a year for comparability of results. NOTE: This requirement applies to tests performed on the same or different instrument makes/
models or by different methods, even if there are different reference intervals or levels of
sensitivity. It includes primary and back up methods used for patient testing. The purpose of the requirement is to evaluate the relationship between test results using different
methodologies, instruments, or testing sites. The laboratory must establish a written procedure for
this check that includes acceptance criteria. This requirement is not applicable to: Calculated parameters Waived methods Laboratories with different CAP numbers
The following types of materials may be used to generate data for comparability studies: Patient/client specimens (pooled or unpooled) are preferred to avoid potential matrix effects Quality control materials for tests performed on the same instrument platform, with both control materials
and reagents of the same manufacturer and lot number. Alternative protocols based on quality control or reference materials for cases when availability or pre
analytical stability of patient/client specimens is a limiting factor. The materials must be validated (when
applicable) to have the same response as fresh human specimens for the instruments and methods
involved.
results.title: Accreditation2020Top10Deficiencies

checks.requirement: The laboratory tests control specimens in the same manner and by the same personnel as patient samples.
checks.subject: QC Handling
checks.note: NOTE: Personnel who routinely perform patient testing must analyze QC specimens; however, this does not imply that each operator must perform QC daily. Personnel must participate in QC on a regular basis. To the extent possible, all steps of the testing process must be controlled.
checks.evidence_of_compliance:
Evidence of Compliance: 
  
  * Records reflecting that QC is run by the same personnel performing patient testing
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Partial. The laboratory has established policy requirements for personnel to adhere to quality control procedures as documented in '5-D1001.5V2-Test personnel job description and responsibilities-CW.docx' and 'G1003.0V5-Laboratory Analytical Phase Quality Control Plan.pdf'. While the IQCP documentation ('XYZ-MOL-Micro-IQCP-Simplexa.docx') confirms that QC is performed regularly, the specific records linking individual testing personnel to the performance of QC specimens alongside patient samples were not verified in the provided documentation. To meet the requirement, the lab must demonstrate that the personnel performing patient testing are the same individuals performing the QC, as required by the MIC.11015 note.
corrective_actions: 1) Implement a documentation log or audit trail that captures the identity of the technologist performing QC alongside the corresponding patient sample batch runs.
2) Conduct a retrospective review of existing QC logs to verify that the personnel performing QC match the personnel listed on patient test reports.
cited_documents: G1003.0V5-Laboratory Analytical Phase Quality Control Plan.pdf
checks.ai_evidence_summary: **MIC.11015**: Testing personnel are responsible for adhering to the laboratory's quality control policies, performing and documenting all QC activities, including instrument and procedural calibrations, Lot to Lot QC of reagents and consumables, and preventive maintenance. They must also perform proficiency tests and maintain records to demonstrate that proficiency testing samples are tested in the same manner as patient specimens. Quality control samples are to be run in the same manner as patient samples, following manufacturer guidelines and SOPs. The quality control samples must react to the examining system similarly to patient samples and have a concentration within the same range as patient samples. The laboratory's Quality Control Plan, G1003.0V5-Laboratory Analytical Phase Quality Control Plan, outlines procedures for control samples, including independent testing of lab-developed controls and lot or shipment QC control for commercial or in-house samples. The plan also details actions for QC failures, including repeating tests and conducting root cause investigations. The XYZ-MOL-Micro-IQCP-Simplexa indicates that training of personnel, including new technologists, is documented in personnel folders. However, records reflecting that QC is run by the same personnel performing patient testing were not found in the provided documents.

XYZ Lab Document Number G1003.0 Version # 5 Author： XYZ Lab Date of Inception: 11/02/2020 Date of Execution of this version：04/26/2026 Page 2 of 4 1.4.1 The lab developed control samples must satisfy the requirement outlined in 1.3, and, prior to put to use, must be
tested independently for at least 5 times and no discordance is found. 1.4.2 Both commercial or in-house quality control samples are subjected to lot or shipment QC control (refer to section 2). The quality control samples used in the assay can be diluted from the original stocks and recorded in G1003.3. The diluted
quality control samples are assigned a new lot number, storage condition and expiration date, and subjected to lot or
shipment QC control as well prior to usage. Lot or shipment control test shall be recorded in the same form (G1003.3). 1.5 In case of QC failure, the following actions shall be taken to determine whether the patient test results from the same
batch can be reported. 1.5.1 Repeat the test with the same control sample. If the repeated control test results fall within the established limits, it
indicates that the previous QC failure is a random event.

policy_evidence.snippet: There were 25 batches running 25 days with number of samples ranging from 2 to 40 each day with both external controls running on each of the testing day during this period. There were not any QC problems. No contamination or deterioration of QC materials were observed. It is in this period we found that we have many negative samples in our testing cohort which could act as a negative control for any potential contamination that an external negative control is used to control. We thus would like to remove the negative external control, and use only positive external control on daily basis provided that there must be at least one sample tested negative for the daily batch. If none negative sample is tested, a NTC sample must be run on that day. Processes to mitigate patient reporting errors based on use of unacceptable specimens or suboptimal test reagents or conditions are addressed in this IQCP. checks.subject: QC Confirmation of Acceptability
checks.evidence_of_compliance:
Evidence of Compliance: 
  
  * Records of control result approval
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Compliant. The laboratory has established a formal process for the review and approval of quality control results prior to the release of patient data. As detailed in the search summary, the 'Sample Control Software Validation Report' (IS1001.SOP) confirms the existence of a 'QC Results' module that requires authorized users to explicitly approve or deny results. The Laboratory Analytical Phase Quality Control Plan further mandates that a supervisor or authorized user (distinct from the testing personnel) must review results for performance acceptance against manufacturer criteria. These procedures satisfy the requirement for documented control result approval.
corrective_actions: Continue current practice of utilizing the QC Results module in the sample control software to document supervisory review and approval of all control results prior to reporting.
cited_documents: IS1001.SOP Sample Control Software Validation Report 240405.pdf
checks.ai_evidence_summary: **MIC.11017**: The Sample Control Software Validation Report outlines a "QC Results" module where users can approve or deny results by selecting a check mark or 'x' mark, respectively. This action marks results as approved or denied on the results report panel. The Laboratory Analytical Phase Quality Control Plan states that experiment results are to be reviewed by a lab supervisor for performance acceptance, following the manufacturer's QC instructions to establish acceptance criteria. All results are QC'd by a trained and authorized user who is not the testing personnel. Quality control records are retained for two years.
