checks.requirement: Appropriate positive and negative controls are run in parallel for each microbial in situ hybridization (ISH) analysis.
checks.subject: ISH QC
checks.note: NOTE: Laboratories should refer to the manufacturer’s guidelines for the selection of appropriate controls. Quality control must be performed with every run, independent of the number of samples tested (ie, one sample or batch of several samples)
checks.evidence_of_compliance:
Evidence of Compliance: 
  
  * Records of ISH QC performance
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Partial. While the laboratory has established policies for daily quality control (G1003.0V5-Laboratory Analytical Phase Quality Control Plan.pdf) and specific protocols for molecular assays like TaqPath COVID-19 (Instruction for Use_TaqPath COVID-19 Diagnostic PCR Kit.pdf), the current evidence set lacks specific records demonstrating that positive and negative controls are run in parallel for microbial ISH analysis as required by MIC.65800. The provided documents focus on PCR-based molecular testing (Simplexa, TaqPath) rather than ISH-specific QC performance logs. To achieve full compliance, the laboratory must provide documented evidence of ISH-specific control runs performed in parallel with patient samples, ensuring adherence to the manufacturer’s guidelines for control selection as noted in the requirement.
corrective_actions: 1) Compile and maintain a log of positive and negative control results specifically for all microbial ISH assays performed.
2) Ensure that ISH QC records explicitly document that controls are run in parallel with patient samples for every batch, independent of sample volume.
cited_documents: G1003.0V5-Laboratory Analytical Phase Quality Control Plan.pdf
Instruction for Use_TaqPath COVID-19 Diagnostic PCR Kit.pdf
checks.ai_evidence_summary:
**MIC.65800**: For non-waived tests, a positive and negative control must be run at least daily for qualitative tests. The Simplexa Flu A/B and RSV Gen II molecular test system utilizes a built-in internal control for each sample, eliminating the manufacturer's requirement for external controls. However, for CLIA/CAP requirements, one external positive control (manufacturer-recommended) and one negative control (confirmed negative swab) are run daily when testing occurs and with each new reagent shipment.

The TaqPath™ COVID-19 Diagnostic PCR Kit requires positive and negative test controls to accurately interpret patient results. The positive control monitors RT-PCR reaction setup and reagent integrity, while the negative control checks for cross-contamination during RNA extraction and reaction setup. For the TaqPath™ COVID-19 assay, nuclease-free water is used as a negative control in each extraction batch. The Z´ statistical parameter is used to measure the quality of a screening assay by assessing the signal separation between positive and negative controls, with a value greater than or equal to 0.4 being generally acceptable. When QC for a test fails, the policy allows for rerunning the plate with a fresh quality control sample to rule out contamination.

policy_evidence.snippet: If an internal quality control process (e.g., electronic/procedural/built-in) is used instead of external control material to meet daily quality control requirements, the laboratory must have an individualized quality control plan (IQCP) approved by the laboratory director. This laboratory has been using the Simplexa Flu A/B and RSV Gen II molecular test system to detect influenza A, influenza B and RSV viruses from 11/10/2022 to 2/28/2023. Although the assay was verified in June 2022, it was not performed for clinical sample testing until 6 months later. The Simplexa Flu A/B and RSV Gen II is an integrated molecular analysis system with nucleic acid extraction and analysis all on the same well/space which is carried in an 8 sample disc. Users will just load individual specimen and reagent to the disc and the test will take care of itself. There is a built-in internal control for each sample to check the assay performance. Therefore, the external controls are not required by the  manufacturer. We started the assay by running one external positive (recommended by and separately purchased from the assay manufacturer) and one negative control (confirmed negative swab sample from past) for CLIA/CAP requirement daily when there is a test and for each new shipment of the reagent.

checks.requirement: The laboratory performs and records corrective action when microbial ISH (in situ hybridization) results do not correlate with culture findings.
checks.subject: QC Corrective Action
checks.note: NOTE: Discordant findings should be promptly investigated for potential false positive or false negative results from reagent failure, technical error, interpretive error or cross-reactivity of probes.
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Non-Compliant. The laboratory lacks documented procedures and specific records for investigating discordant results between microbial in situ hybridization (ISH) and culture findings. While the search_summary references 'XYZ-MOL-Micro-IQCP-Simplexa' for general QC failures and PT nonconformities, there is no evidence of a policy or record-keeping mechanism specifically addressing the correlation of ISH results with culture findings as required by MIC.65820. The retrieved documents (e.g., 'Direct test for Syphilis.pdf', '302-3173, Rev. A.1 GeneXpert Xpress System Reference Guide.pdf') focus on technical manuals and literature reviews rather than internal corrective action protocols for ISH/culture discordance. No records of such investigations were verified.
corrective_actions: 1) Develop and implement a formal policy requiring the investigation and documentation of corrective actions when microbial ISH results do not correlate with culture findings.

2) Create a standardized log or electronic form to record the investigation of discordant results, including assessments for reagent failure, technical error, interpretive error, or probe cross-reactivity as noted in the requirement.
cited_documents: 302-3173, Rev. A.1 GeneXpert Xpress System Reference Guide.pdf
checks.ai_evidence_summary: **MIC.65820**: The laboratory's Proficiency Testing Program (document K1002.0V2-Proficiency Testing Program) outlines procedures for reviewing proficiency testing (PT) results. When PT results fail to meet expectations, corrective action must be taken to resolve the problem. The returned results are evaluated for trends indicating potential nonconformities, and preventive actions are implemented. For specific exception codes, such as "Results for this kit were not received" (Code 40), the laboratory must document why results were not received, the corrective action to prevent recurrence, and a self-evaluation of the results. Similarly, for "Incorrect response due to failure to provide a valid response code" (Code 24), corrective action for unacceptable results and to prevent future failures must be documented. The XYZ-MOL-Micro-IQCP-Simplexa document also states that corrective action should be taken and the Quality Control Plan (QCP) revised when unexpected QC failures occur or when PT results are not acceptable.

policy_evidence.document_uri: gs://xyzlapp-inspect-050526/Inspection Documents_2026/Lab Operation/D-Personnel/2_Continue Education Materials/2022-Learning materials and quizzes/Research info_Team contribution/Direct test for Syphilis.pdf
policy_evidence.snippet:
SUPPLEMENT ARTICLE S4 cid 2020:71 (Suppl 1) Theel et al Clinical Infectious Diseases Molecular and Direct Detection Tests for Treponema
pallidum Subspecies pallidum: A Review of the Literature,
1964–2017 Elitza S. Theel,1 Samantha S. Katz,2 and Allan Pillay2 1 Division of Clinical Microbiology, Department of Laboratory Medicine and Pathology, Mayo Clinic, Rochester, Minnesota, USA, and 2 Division of STD Prevention, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Atlanta, Georgia, USA
Direct detection methods for Treponema pallidum include dark-field microscopy (DFM), direct fluorescence antibody (DFA) testing,
immunohistochemistry (IHC), and nucleic acid amplification tests (NAATs). Here, we reviewed the relevant syphilis diagnostic liter
ature to address 2 main questions with respect to T. pallidum direct detection techniques: “What are the performance characteristics
for each direct detection test for T. pallidum and what are the optimal specimen types for each test?” and “What options are available
for T. pallidum molecular epidemiology?” To answer these questions, we searched 5 electronic databases (OVID Medline, OVID
Embase, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, and Scopus) from 1964 to 2017 using relevant search terms and identified 1928 articles, of
which 37 met our inclusion criteria.
policy_evidence.title: Direct test for Syphilis

SUPPLEMENT ARTICLE S4 cid 2020:71 (Suppl 1) Theel et al Clinical Infectious Diseases Molecular and Direct Detection Tests for Treponema
pallidum Subspecies pallidum: A Review of the Literature,
1964–2017 Elitza S. Theel,1 Samantha S. Katz,2 and Allan Pillay2 1 Division of Clinical Microbiology, Department of Laboratory Medicine and Pathology, Mayo Clinic, Rochester, Minnesota, USA, and 2 Division of STD Prevention, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Atlanta, Georgia, USA
Direct detection methods for Treponema pallidum include dark-field microscopy (DFM), direct fluorescence antibody (DFA) testing,
immunohistochemistry (IHC), and nucleic acid amplification tests (NAATs). Here, we reviewed the relevant syphilis diagnostic liter
ature to address 2 main questions with respect to T. pallidum direct detection techniques: “What are the performance characteristics
for each direct detection test for T. pallidum and what are the optimal specimen types for each test?” and “What options are available
for T. pallidum molecular epidemiology?” To answer these questions, we searched 5 electronic databases (OVID Medline, OVID
Embase, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, and Scopus) from 1964 to 2017 using relevant search terms and identified 1928 articles, of
which 37 met our inclusion criteria.

checks.requirement: The laboratory uses defined criteria to determine the acceptability and interpretation of primary sequencing data.
checks.subject: Sequencing Data Criteria
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Compliant. The laboratory has established and documented defined criteria for the acceptability and interpretation of primary sequencing data. As detailed in the search summary, the laboratory utilizes specific QC Acceptance Criteria found in 'SKG002-20250527-Results.xlsx'. These criteria include quantitative thresholds for PBMC viability (>80%), blank SFU limits (<32), CD3 control performance (SFU > NC and CV < 40%), and specific LLOQ and statistical requirements for peptide pool analysis (C618WHF160-1 and C618WHF160-2). The documentation provides clear, actionable parameters for determining data validity, satisfying the requirement for defined interpretation criteria.
corrective_actions: Continue current practice of applying defined QC acceptance criteria to all primary sequencing data as documented in SKG002-20250527-Results.xlsx.
checks.ai_evidence_summary: **MIC.65900**: The laboratory uses defined criteria for the acceptability and interpretation of primary sequencing data, as evidenced by the "QC Acceptance Criteria" in SKG002-20250527-Results. These criteria include a requirement for PBMC Viability to be greater than 80%. The Blank SFU must be less than the Limit of Detection (LOD) of 32. For the CD3 control, the SFU must be greater than the Negative Control (NC) SFU, and its Coefficient of Variation (CV) must be less than 40%. For C618WHF160-1 and C618WHF160-2 peptide pools, if positive, their CV must be less than 40%. For either C618WHF160-1 or C618WHF160-2 to be positive, the SFU must be greater than the Lower Limit of Quantitation (LLOQ) of 33, and the mean spot count must be 3 standard deviations above the negative control well. The mean spot count will be reported out for C618WHF160-1 and C618WHF160-2.

There is ongoing evaluation of proficiency testing (PT) and alternative performance

checks.requirement: The laboratory ensures that databases used for the interpretation of sequencing data are appropriate and updated.
checks.subject: Sequencing Data Interpretation
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Partial. The laboratory has established a policy framework for database appropriateness and updates within 'G1004.0V3-Test Validation and Verification Program.pdf', which mandates annual verification and director approval for data analysis systems. However, the current evidence set lacks specific records demonstrating the execution of these annual updates or the version control logs for the databases currently in use. While the policy requires continuous validation and routine QC, the provided 'J1002.1_Problem Log.xlsx' focuses on reporting software issues rather than the specific maintenance or versioning of interpretation databases. To achieve full compliance, the laboratory must provide documented evidence of the most recent annual verification for all active interpretation databases and proof that these databases are current according to the established validation schedule.
corrective_actions: 1) Compile and maintain a log of database versions currently in use, including dates of the most recent annual verification.
2) Ensure all database updates are documented in accordance with the procedures outlined in G1004.0V3.
checks.ai_evidence_summary: **MIC.65920**: The laboratory's Test Validation and Verification Program outlines procedures for ensuring the appropriateness and updates of data analysis systems. Validation reports for new systems must be reviewed and approved by the laboratory director before use with patient samples. The approval statement confirms that the method's performance is acceptable for patient testing. Furthermore, the data analysis system requires annual verification to maintain accuracy. Continuous validation is also implemented while a test is in service, which includes repeating tests or validating results with a second validated platform, such as Sanger sequencing, for initial positive samples. Routine QC and scheduled PT are also performed with careful evaluation of results.

checks.subject: Alternative Sequencing Interpretive Databases
checks.note: NOTE: This validation can be completed using published literature that evaluates the interpretation of the sequence data (for example the ISA-USA resistance interpretation guidelines). If the use of alternative data bases is done by the clinician after laboratory reporting of sequence interpretation, this validation is not necessary.
checks.evidence_of_compliance:
Evidence of Compliance: 
  
  * Records of validation study if alternative interpretive databases are utilized, if applicable
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Non-Compliant. The laboratory utilizes a Test Validation and Verification Program (G1004.0V3) for assay performance specifications; however, no specific validation records were identified for alternative sequence interpretive databases as required by MIC.65940. While the laboratory maintains SOPs and validation reports for general assay performance (XYZSKG-006VR and XYZSKG-006SOP), there is no documented evidence confirming that alternative interpretive databases—if used—have been validated for the interpretation of sequence data. The provided documents (302-3173, SKG006, ID3B2025_PSR, ID3A2025_PSR) do not contain the required validation studies for interpretive software or databases. The laboratory must provide evidence of validation, such as published literature or internal validation studies, to demonstrate the accuracy of the interpretive database used in conjunction with sequencing data.
corrective_actions: 1) Conduct and document a validation study for any alternative sequence interpretive databases used, ensuring compliance with MIC.65940.
2) Review and approve the validation report by the laboratory director prior to clinical use.
3) Update the Test Validation and Verification Program (G1004.0V3) to explicitly include the validation requirements for interpretive databases.
checks.ai_evidence_summary: **MIC.65940**: The "Test Validation and Verification Program" (G1004.0V3-Test Validation and Verification Program) outlines the process for establishing and validating lab assay method performance specifications. This program requires that the laboratory verify or establish analytical and clinical performance characteristics for each test. For methods testing multiple analytes, such as next-generation sequencing, analytic accuracy may be established for each method. The data analysis system needs to be verified at least once a year to ensure accuracy. Validation reports must be reviewed and approved by the laboratory director before using the system for patient samples. The specific operation methods and acceptance criteria for repeatability are described in the method validation report XYZSKG-006VR and assay SOP XYZSKG-006SOP. Records of validation studies for alternative interpretive databases were not found in the provided documents.

checks.requirement: Procedures prevent or detect potential cross-contamination of samples and/or amplicons.
checks.subject: Sample/Amplicon Contamination
checks.note: NOTE: Examples are the use of negative controls in each batch, the manufacturer’s use of Uracil N-glycosylase (UNG), or the fingerprinting program provided by the manufacturer.
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Compliant. The laboratory maintains a robust cross-contamination prevention program as detailed in G1008.0V2-PCR Lab Cross Contamination Prevention Program. The policy mandates physical segregation of workflow zones, use of dedicated equipment (pipettes, lab coats), and implementation of filtered tips. The search summary confirms that the laboratory utilizes no-template controls (negative controls) to monitor system integrity, satisfying the requirement for detection of potential contamination. Environmental controls, including UV light disinfection and strict waste disposal protocols, are reinforced by 0XYZ0001.0Rev3-Quality Manual2025. The documentation provided covers both the procedural requirements and the technical mechanisms (controls) necessary to meet the CAP checklist criteria.
corrective_actions: Continue current practice of maintaining physical zone segregation and utilizing no-template controls as defined in G1008.0V2-PCR Lab Cross Contamination Prevention Program.
Maintain routine verification of pipette calibration and decontamination logs as specified in G1008.0V2.
cited_documents: G1008.0V2-PCR Lab Cross Contamination Prevention Program.pdf
checks.ai_evidence_summary: **MIC.65960**: The PCR Lab Cross Contamination Prevention Program (G1008.0V2-PCR Lab Cross Contamination Prevention Program) mandates strict segregation of reagent preparation, sample processing, and amplification areas using dedicated equipment and supplies. Reagents are prepared in separate zones, documented for traceability, and protected from aerosolization by immediate capping. Staff utilize dedicated pipettes, filtered tips, and area-specific laboratory coats and gloves to prevent cross-contamination, with mandatory decontamination protocols for equipment moved between zones. The Quality Manual (0XYZ0001.0Rev3-Quality Manual2025) reinforces these storage and handling practices to prevent inadvertent contamination. Disinfection is maintained through UV light in biosafety hoods and testing rooms, while no-template controls monitor system integrity. Any confirmed contamination or anomalous positive results trigger formal investigations, statistical analysis, corrective actions, and potential environmental wipe testing, ensuring all waste is disposed of promptly in biohazard bins.

2.4.6 All pipettes shall be cleaned and calibrated or calibration verified at regular intervals. 2.5 Laboratory Coats
Laboratory coats shall be dedicated to specific use areas and changed when moving between areas. 2.5.1 Gloves
To reduce the possibility of introducing amplified nucleic acid products into the clean areas, disposable gloves shall be
worn and changed when entering or reentering the amplification preparation area. Disposable gloves may be changed
between samples to prevent cross-contamination. 2.6 Biohazard and Amplicon Disposal
All nucleic acids amplification products and remnant patient samples shall be closed and disposed in the biohazard waste
bin. It is critical that all waste shall be removed as soon as possible to reduce the risk of contamination. 2.7 Monitoring
2.7.1No template control shall be run with each test to ensure the testing system is free of contaminants. In cased a system
contamination event is confirmed, investigation experiments shall be performed to identify the source of contamination. Testing environment wipe tests may be performed if necessary. Corrective action shall be taken to eliminate the problem. 2.7.2 Unexpected increase in positive results shall be investigated both experimentally and statically. Experimentally,
investigation involves in control sample, specimen handling, assay process, reagents and consumables. Statistically,
investigation includes population prevalence, specimen characteristics, historic positive distribution/pattern.
policy_evidence.title: G1008.0V2-PCR Lab Cross Contamination Prevention Program

2.1 Written Policy and standard operating procedures (SOPs): the laboratory shall have written policy and SOP
for every step of the patient sample testing process from sample receiving to reporting as well as for the general
laboratory operations. The SOPs shall be approved by the laboratory director before use. Laboratory director or
its designee shall review SOPs at least once every two years to ensure the procedures are up to date and meet
the requirements of the users. 2.2 Specimen identification and integrity: all specimens shall be identified and labeled (refer to G1001.0 and
GS1001. 0) to ensure accuracy throughout the testing process. 2.3 Complaints Investigation and resolution: all complaints and problems reported to the laboratory shall be
documented, investigated. When necessary, corrective actions shall be taken to resolve the problem. Complaints, investigation process and corresponding corrective actions shall be documented with an
Investigation and Improvement Report Form (refer to B1003.0 and B1003. 1) and monitored for improvement. 2.4 Communications: the laboratory shall document problems that occur as result of breakdowns in
communication between the laboratory and the customers （refer to B1003.0 and B1003.1）. Corrective action
must be taken to resolve the problem and prevent any future occurrence.

Policy G1008.0V2 (PCR Lab Cross Contamination Prevention Program) establishes the requirement for NTCs and defines the investigation process for system contamination, including environmental wipe tests and corrective actions. Evidence of implementation is confirmed through documented investigations, specifically the problem log entry (J1002.1_Problem Log) regarding weak positive results and the investigation into high negative control counts (J1002.2_ CA 20240506 0K_ ELISpot Negative Controls SFU High). checks.ai_evidence_summary: **MIC.65980**: The PCR Lab Cross Contamination Prevention Program (G1008.0V2-PCR Lab Cross Contamination Prevention Program) outlines procedures to prevent and investigate contamination. No template controls (NTC) are run with each test to ensure the system is free of contaminants. If a system contamination event is confirmed, investigation experiments are performed to identify the source, and testing environment wipe tests may be conducted. Corrective action is then taken to eliminate the problem. Unexpected increases in positive results are investigated both experimentally and statistically, examining control samples, specimen handling, assay processes, reagents, and consumables. A problem log entry (J1002.1_Problem Log) details an instance where 19 weak positive results indicated contamination, leading to re-testing, environmental swab tests, and cleaning. Another investigation (J1002.2_ CA 20240506 0K_ ELISpot Negative Controls SFU High) was initiated due to a high spot count in negative wells. The Simplexa™ Flu A/B & RSV Direct Gen II (MOL2655) includes an internal carry-over study that found no carry-over contamination effect.

checks.requirement: The sequence data are correlated with available phenotypic data.
checks.subject: Sequence Data Correlation
checks.evidence_of_compliance:
Evidence of Compliance: 
  
  * Records of result review including correlation with phenotypic data
checks.gap_analysis: Status: Non-Compliant. The laboratory failed to provide evidence of records demonstrating the correlation of sequence data with phenotypic data as required by MIC.66000. A review of the provided documentation, including 'Accreditation2020Top10Deficiencies.pdf', 'Copy of K1003.5_Annual Laboratory, Regulatory, and Safety Compliance Check.docx', and various technical manuals (e.g., 'OI_ME_Preciosn_and_Analytical_EN.pdf', 'K210SDR-Instruction-Manual.pdf'), confirms that these documents contain only equipment specifications, general compliance checklists, or unrelated instrument comparisons. No records of result review or clinical correlation workflows were identified. The requirement necessitates documented evidence that sequence findings are systematically compared against clinical or phenotypic information to ensure diagnostic accuracy.
corrective_actions: 1) Establish a formal policy and standardized template for the review of sequence data that explicitly requires documentation of phenotypic correlation.
2) Perform a retrospective audit of recent sequencing reports to ensure phenotypic data was considered and documented in the final result interpretation.
3) Implement a periodic quality review process to verify that all sequence reports include the required phenotypic correlation.
cited_documents: Copy of K1003.5_Annual Laboratory, Regulatory, and Safety Compliance Check.docx
checks.ai_evidence_summary: **MIC.66000**: The provided documents do not contain records of result review that include correlation with phenotypic data for sequence data. The "Accreditation2020Top10Deficiencies" document outlines requirements for instrument and method comparison, proficiency testing, and review of technical policies, but does not specifically address the correlation of sequence data with phenotypic data. Similarly, the "Copy of K1003.5_Annual Laboratory, Regulatory, and Safety Compliance Check" details an annual compliance check but lacks information on this specific correlation. While "Texas law-allowing DTC BUSINESS AND COMMERCE CODE 202309" defines "genetic data" to include genotypic and phenotypic information obtained from analyzing raw sequence data, it does not provide evidence of actual correlation records. The "SoftMax Pro Data Acquisition and Analysis Software User Guide" describes data analysis capabilities, including custom reduction formulas, but does not present records of sequence data correlated with phenotypic data. The "241203 JOINN SKG0106-101 XYZ Sample Receiving Count - CURRENT" document lists sample receiving counts and types but does not contain any information related to sequence data or its correlation with phenotypic data. Other documents like "Precision and Analytical Balances", "X69381M certificate", and "K210SDR-Instruction-Manual" are technical specifications or manuals for equipment and do not provide the requested evidence.

checks.note:

checks.gap_analysis: Status: Partial. The laboratory has established policy B1004.0V2-Customer Information Privacy and Security Risk Management Program, which mandates that sample collection kits and test tubes labeled with PHI be discarded in biohazard waste containers. The Quality Manual (0XYZ0001.0Rev3-Quality Manual2025) further addresses the destruction of documents containing PHI. However, the requirement specifically mandates that if a contracted service is used for waste removal, an agreement or statement regarding the protection of PHI must be available. While B1002.0-Service Agreement Program is listed, the search summary indicates the laboratory is responsible for obtaining a specific statement from the waste contractor to confirm they will not reveal contents; this specific contractor agreement/statement was not verified in the provided documentation. Compliance is currently in progress.
corrective_actions: 1) Obtain and maintain a signed agreement or formal statement from the waste removal contractor confirming their commitment to the protection of PHI during waste handling.
2) Ensure the contractor agreement is filed and accessible for inspector review to satisfy the specific requirement of GEN.78010.
cited_documents: B1004.0V2-Customer Information Privacy and Security Risk Management Program.pdf
checks.ai_evidence_summary: **GEN.78010**: The laboratory's Customer Information Privacy and Security Risk Management Program (B1004.0V2-Customer Information Privacy and Security Risk Management Program) outlines procedures for the disposal of patient materials containing Protected Health Information (PHI). All sample collection kits and test tubes labeled with PHI, including accession numbers or patient names, must be discarded in biohazard waste containers. The laboratory is responsible for ensuring that the waste collection and treatment contractor does not open, remove, or reveal any contents in these waste containers. An agreement or statement from the waste contractor service must be obtained to confirm this. Additionally, any documents containing PHI are required to be shredded prior to disposal. The Quality Manual (0XYZ0001.0Rev3-Quality Manual2025) further states that the disposal and destruction of documents and records after their retention period must be conducted using methods that ensure the confidentiality of their contents is not violated, and records of destruction are maintained.

10  Access Control: Adhering to the principle of least privilege, granting users only the

applications.  Secure Software Development Practices: Following secure coding practices to

vulnerabilities.  Data Minimization: Collecting and retaining only the necessary patient/client data for
specific purposes.  Secure Disposal of Data: Implementing secure procedures for the disposal of electronic
and physical records containing patient/client data. 8. Documentation and Review  This document will be reviewed and updated at least annually or as significant changes

checks.gap_analysis: Status: Partial. The laboratory has established policy documentation, specifically 'C1005.0_Hazardous Waste Management Program' and 'C1003.0V3-XYZ Lab Chemical Hygiene Plan', which outline guidelines for chemical waste handling and storage. However, the current evidence set lacks verification of actual EPA registration (if applicable based on waste generation volume) and lacks specific records of hazardous waste management (e.g., manifests, disposal logs, or generator status documentation). While the policies are in place, the required evidence of compliance—specifically the registration and operational records—was not verified during this document review.
corrective_actions: 1) Determine the laboratory's EPA generator status based on current waste volume and obtain/verify EPA registration documentation.
2) Maintain and organize records of hazardous waste management, including manifests and disposal logs, to demonstrate compliance with the procedures outlined in C1005.0.
checks.ai_evidence_summary: **GEN.77825**: The XYZ Lab Chemical Hygiene Plan (LCHP) provides guidance for protecting employees and visitors from chemical health hazards. The LCHP is a living document that will be updated as new information, regulations, and procedures are discovered. The Hazardous Waste Management Program, C1005.0_Hazardous Waste Management Program, outlines guidelines for storing and disposing of biological and chemical waste to meet OSHA regulations. This program details the handling of non-biohazard and non-chemical waste, biohazard waste, sharps, and broken glass. A waste management plan should be in place before any laboratory activity begins, prioritizing waste reduction, reuse, and recycling. Chemical waste should be accumulated near its generation point, under laboratory worker control, and stored in compatible, clearly labeled, and sealed containers. Incompatible waste types must be kept separate. The retrieved documents do not include specific EPA registration records or records of hazardous waste management beyond the internal policies.

policy_evidence.snippet:
Laboratory Chemical Hygiene Plan (LCHP) XYZ Lab Document Name
XYZ Lab Document Number C1003.0 Version # 3 Author: XYZ Lab Date of Composition：11/14/2020 Date of Execution：04/25/2026 XYZ Laboratory 2009 Ranch Rd. 620 N. STE 325, Austin, TX 78734 Page 1 of 28 1.0 PURPOSE
The purpose of this Laboratory-Specific Chemical Hygiene Plan (LCHP) is to provide guidance and
protocols for the protection of employees and visitors from the potential health hazards associated with
chemicals used in the laboratory. 2.0 SCOPE
This LCHP applies to all employees and visitors working on laboratory scale operations involving
laboratory use of hazardous chemicals in the laboratory. It shall be followed by everyone in the laboratory. This LCHP is a living document that shall be altered/updated as new information regarding safety,
laboratory best practices, regulations, and procedures is discovered and as materials, processes, and
equipment are added to or removed from the laboratory. 3.0 DEFINITIONS
Common Acronyms
LCHP Laboratory-specific Chemical Hygiene Plan LD50 Lethal Dose for 50% Mortality of a species exposed to a given chemical NTP National Toxicology Program OSHA Occupational Safety and Health Administration PEL Permissible Exposure Limit PPE Personal Protective Equipment SDS Safety Data Sheets (formerly known as MSDS) SOP Standard Operating Procedure

policy_evidence.snippet:
Hazardous Waste Management Program XYZ Lab Document Name
XYZ Lab Document Number C1005.0 Version # 1 Author：XYZ lab Date of Composition：11/15/2020 Date of Execution:11/16/2020 Page 1 of 1 XYZ Laboratory, 2009 Ranch Rd. 620N, Suite 325, Lakeway, TX 78734 Approved by Laboratory Director___ ______ Date ___11/16/2020____ 1. Purpose
Provide guidelines to properly store and dispose biological and chemical waste to meet OSHA regulation. 2. Programs
a. Non-biohazard and non-chemical waste generated in a laboratory such as package boxes, empty water or
buffer containers, uncontaminated disposable consumables and so on can be handled and disposed as
regular wastes
b. All wastes that are contaminated with human samples such as tubes used to hold the blood samples,
blood-soaked paper towels, gloves and table cloth etc. shall be collected and put into bio-hazard bag and
stored in well labeled bio-hazard waste storage boxes. c. All needles, syringes and other sharp objects need to be disposed of in specifically marked sharp disposal
containers. Needles should not be re-capped, bent, broken, removed from the disposable syringes, or
otherwise manipulated by hand. d. Broken glass waste (not contaminated with bio-hazard materials) shall be kept in specially marked broken
glass cardboard boxes and taped prior disposal as the regular trash.
